sheet-1.description: Sheet 1 is the north-western corner of the West Orange volume, drawn at 200 feet to an inch. The upper edge follows the dash-dot boundary of Livingston Township. Mount Pleasant Avenue, drawn about 60 feet wide at its southern end, crosses the sheet from the top edge near the right-hand third, runs south-south-west and then bends south-east to reach Pleasant Valley at the bottom right, where a hydrant and a curved corner mark the junction. Pleasant Valley, a 40 foot road, runs along the lower edge and ends at Mountain Avenue, a narrow road that leaves the sheet at the bottom left. Two short parallel lanes, Summit Avenue and Sun Rise Avenue, are laid out as lots west of Mount Pleasant Avenue at about the middle of the sheet. The rest of the sheet is open farmland divided into long lots, with owners' names lettered along them, among them Charles Ringer Est., Wm. E. Condit, G. S. Condit, Geo. Werner, Jacob Roth Jr., Mrs. John Kuhn, Chas. N. White and Geo. Merklen Est.; lot numbers 170 to 173 are printed. Buildings are few and cluster along Mount Pleasant Avenue: the John B. Scarlett farm, a building labelled Mountain Inn near the top, a stone quarry operated by Fusco and Son, and scattered farmhouses. A small pond is drawn near the centre. The north arrow and the title block are at the upper left, and the adjoining sheets are numbered in the corners and margins.
notes: Pleasant Valley is printed here without 'Way'; today it is Pleasant Valley Way.

Mountain Avenue meets Pleasant Valley Way at the lower left; its continuation east of Pleasant Valley Way (sheet 5) is today's Old Indian Road. The part drawn on this sheet leaves the sheet toward the bottom and has no modern counterpart in the street data.
Summit Avenue and Sun Rise Avenue are not in the modern street data and were not used as control.

Only two junctions survive on this sheet (Pleasant Valley Way with Old Indian Road and with Mount Pleasant Avenue); the part is placed by a two-point helmert and the fitted scale is about 2 percent below the 200 ft nominal scale.
West Orange, 200 ft; farms along Pleasant Valley and Mount Pleasant Av, Livingston line at top; two-point helmert, low

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 lies north of sheet 6 and between sheets 1 and 3. The top edge is the Livingston Township line, drawn as a dash-dot line that slopes slightly upward to the right. The sheet is almost entirely farmland: long narrow lots running across the sheet are lettered with owners' names, including D. C. Baker, Arthur D. Crane, Geo. Merklen Est., Chas. N. White, Jacob Merdinger, Anna H. Root Est., B. L. Allen, Albert Williams Est., John K. Jones, Moses E. Condit, Amelia Vincent, Benj. P. Laidlow, F. B. Vincent and J. Rodman Paul, with lot numbers 172 to 175. The only roads are at the lower edge. Pleasant Valley Way, drawn about 40 feet wide, crosses the bottom from left to right with a bend at its junction with Mount Pleasant Place, a 40 foot road leaving the sheet toward the bottom. At the lower left corner Mount Pleasant Avenue, a 60 foot road with a numbered hydrant, comes in from the left and meets Pleasant Valley Way. A fire alarm box and a hydrant stand on Pleasant Valley Way near the lower right, and a six-inch water pipe is drawn in the road. Buildings are few: farm groups near Chas. Ringer Est. at the lower left, near Jacob Merdinger and Moses E. Condit, and near F. B. Vincent at the lower right. The north arrow is at the centre and the title block at the upper right.
notes: Control is two junctions at the lower left (Pleasant Valley Way with Mount Pleasant Avenue and with Mount Pleasant Place) plus a fire alarm box carried from sheet 6; the part is placed by a helmert and is low confidence.
The upper three quarters of the sheet is blank farmland with no street control.
West Orange, 200 ft; farmland, Pleasant Valley Way junctions at lower left; helmert plus a point carried from sheet 6, low

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers farmland in the north of West Orange between the Livingston Township line at the top and Pleasant Valley Way along the bottom. Laurel Avenue, a 40 foot road, enters from the top edge a little left of centre and runs south-east to a Y-shaped junction with Eagle Rock Avenue near the right-hand third of the sheet. Eagle Rock Avenue comes from the top right corner, where the line of the Borough of Essex Fells meets the Livingston Township line, curves southward and then runs down the right side of the sheet to Pleasant Valley Way near the lower right corner. There it is crossed by Pleasant Valley Way, with a fire alarm box and a hydrant at the corner and the German Presbyterian Church on the west side. Pleasant Valley Way runs the length of the lower edge. Large tracts are labelled J. Rodman Paul, with narrower lots for Rosa Wasserman, Leo. P. Heintz, F. Sipple, Martin Ford, Wm. Krouth, Geo. Diefenbacker, Wolff and Hahn, Mrs. W. H. Mosher, W. H. Mayer, Hannah Vincent, Thomas Vincent Est., C. D. Vincent, Henry Vincent, Amelia Vincent, H. R. Chichester and F. B. Vincent. Lot numbers 174 to 177 are printed. Sunnybrook Farm, with long poultry houses, and Pleasantdale Public School stand on Pleasant Valley Way. The north arrow is at the right edge and the title block at the upper left.
notes: The Laurel Avenue and Eagle Rock Avenue Y junction was hand-picked at the centre of the three roads; it is the same corner as at the left edge of sheet 4.
Control is this Y junction and Eagle Rock Avenue with Pleasant Valley Way, 7000 px apart; the part is placed by a helmert and is low confidence.
Several of the modern streets near Eagle Rock Avenue (Shrump Place, Sherwood Place, Oak Terrace) were laid out after 1912 and are not drawn.
West Orange, 200 ft; Eagle Rock Av, Laurel Av, Pleasant Valley Way; Essex Fells and Livingston lines; helmert, low

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 is the north-eastern sheet of the West Orange 200 foot series and lies east of sheet 3. The Borough of Essex Fells line runs across the top edge, sloping slightly downward to the right. Eagle Rock Avenue, a 50 foot road, runs down the left side of the sheet from the top left corner, with Laurel Avenue joining it at the left edge near the upper left, and meets Pleasant Valley Way at the bottom left, where a fire alarm box, a hydrant and the Pleasantdale Hotel stand. Pleasant Valley Way then runs east along the lower edge, bending south-east toward the bottom right corner. The sheet is mostly farmland divided into long lots lettered with the names of James W. Paul Jr., J. Rodman Paul, Ira H. Condit Est., John Warner, Fred Schrump, Peter Schmitt, John F. Wolff, Charlotte W. Hopkins, Isabella Hopkins, and Catherine Hopkins; lot numbers 176 to 179 are printed. The Pleasant Valley Quarry, with power, steam and lighting apparatus, stands beside Eagle Rock Avenue in the left part of the sheet, and farm buildings line Pleasant Valley Way. The north arrow is at the right and the title block at the upper right; the neighbouring sheets are numbered 3, 8 and 9 around the margins.
notes: Control is Eagle Rock Avenue with Pleasant Valley Way at the lower left and the Laurel Avenue Y junction at the left edge (hand-picked, same corner as on sheet 3); the part is placed by a helmert and is low confidence.
The two sheets 3 and 4 differ by about 2 degrees in drawn rotation.
West Orange, 200 ft; Eagle Rock Av, Pleasant Valley Way; helmert from two points, low

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 lies south of sheet 1 and is drawn turned about a quarter turn from it, so that Pleasant Valley Way runs down the left edge. Mount Pleasant Avenue, a 60 foot road, runs along the top of the sheet from the upper left, where it leaves the sheet diagonally, to Prospect Avenue at the right edge. Saint Cloud Avenue, a 40 foot road, branches from it at a hydrant and fire alarm box and runs straight down the sheet to Mountain Avenue. Mountain Avenue, drawn about 50 feet wide, runs across the lower part of the sheet from Pleasant Valley Way on the left, bends twice near the middle and continues south-east to Prospect Avenue at the lower right. A small stream, unlabelled, runs down the left side of the sheet from Mount Pleasant Avenue to a pond-like end near the bottom. The sheet is mostly farm and estate land lettered with owners' names, among them Catherine R. Condit, Wm. E. Condit, William E. Condit, John P. Condit, Christina Young, Douglas Robinson, Herbert Austin, Joseph N. Condit, Irene Scott Brown, Maclay Association Inc., John Crosby Brown, Marie Louise Scott, Mary L. Scott, Harriet D. W. Whitmore and Chas. Hersheim. Lot numbers 156 and 157 are printed. Buildings are sparse and stand along Mount Pleasant Avenue and Mountain Avenue. The north arrow is at the centre and the title block at the upper left.
notes: Mountain Avenue is today's Old Indian Road; it was identified from the spacing of its junctions with Pleasant Valley Way, Saint Cloud Avenue and Prospect Avenue.
Saint Cloud Avenue does not reach Mount Pleasant Avenue in the modern street data; its junction with Mount Pleasant Avenue was not used.
The junctions with Prospect Avenue lie at the right edge of the sheet and were hand-picked from the drawn left edge of Prospect Avenue plus half of its 60 ft width.
The sheet is turned about 90 degrees from sheets 1 to 4, rotation about -24 degrees.
West Orange, 200 ft, turned about 90 degrees; Mount Pleasant, Saint Cloud, Mountain Av (today Old Indian Road), Prospect; medium-low

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 lies south of sheet 2 and east of sheet 5. Pleasant Valley Way, a 40 foot road, crosses the top of the sheet from upper left to upper right, rising gently, with a fire alarm box near the right end. At the upper left it meets Mount Pleasant Avenue, a 60 foot road with a numbered hydrant, and Mount Pleasant Place, a 40 foot road labelled Mt. Pleasant Av. that runs down to Saint Cloud Avenue. Saint Cloud Avenue crosses the left part of the sheet at a fire alarm box. Mount Pleasant Avenue runs down the whole left edge of the sheet to its junction with Prospect Avenue at the lower left, and Prospect Avenue then runs east across the bottom, rising to the right. Marcella Avenue, a narrow road, leaves it southward near the bottom left. A winding brook crosses the upper part of the sheet from left to right and then turns south, with a pond-shaped end near the bottom. Mount Pleasant School No. 5, with heat, steam and electric light noted, stands near Saint Cloud Avenue. The remainder is farm and estate land lettered with the names of Chas. Ringer Est., D. T. Edwards, W. N. Williams, Orlando Williams, John R. Vincent, Moses E. Condit, John B. Schultz, Geo. Schultz, Edward S. Dodd, A. Miller, Lillian E. Hedden, Ira A. Kipp Jr. et al., Wm. Parkinson Est., Mrs. Theodore Reynolds and Julius Eckert. Lot numbers 153 to 157 are printed.
notes: The 40 foot road from Pleasant Valley Way to Saint Cloud Avenue, labelled Mt. Pleasant Av. here, is today's Mount Pleasant Place; Mount Pleasant Place meets Mount Pleasant Avenue at the Saint Cloud Avenue crossing in the modern data.
Marcella Avenue is the name printed on the sheet; it is today's Marcella Avenue.
The part is turned about 90 degrees from sheet 5, rotation about +62 degrees.
West Orange, 200 ft; Mount Pleasant Av and Place, Pleasant Valley Way, Prospect, Marcella; medium

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 is drawn at 200 feet to an inch and covers the thinly settled northern part of West Orange between Pleasant Valley Way and Prospect Avenue. Pleasant Valley Way crosses the top of the sheet from the left edge to the upper right corner, where it meets Eagle Rock Avenue. Eagle Rock Avenue then runs down the right side of the sheet, bending south-west and then south to meet Prospect Avenue at the foot of the sheet. Prospect Avenue enters at the lower left, curves along the bottom and ends at the Eagle Rock Avenue crossing, where the sheet is marked with a fire alarm box. Almost all of the ground is drawn as large farm and estate parcels labelled with their owners, among them the Thos. Vincent estate, Charles D. Vincent, Fred W. Wolff, Elizabeth Halm, Lillie C. Arlt, P. W. Kennady, Emma L. Mayes, Edward S. Dodd, Thos. B. Blackburn, Michael Rosney, Mary Fundus and Hugh Mitchell. Vincent's Pond and its feeder stream fill the upper left, with a small pump house at the pond. A small cemetery and the house of T. Hoffman stand on the east side of Eagle Rock Avenue. Dwellings, barns and outbuildings are few and are scattered along the main roads. Along the right edge several short streets of the Eagle Rock Terrace tract (Forest, Eagle, Redwood and Henry) and Terrace Avenue leave Eagle Rock Avenue and continue on sheet 8. Water pipe and the elevation of the roads are marked along Pleasant Valley Way and Prospect Avenue. The compass rose at the top is turned about 50 degrees, so north lies toward the upper right.
notes: Forest Avenue is cut by the right edge of the sheet and its suffix is partly lost; read as Forest Av. from sheet 8, where it is printed in full.
Printed Forest Road is the modern Forest Avenue; Eagle Street and the other Eagle Rock Terrace side streets are not in OpenStreetMap.
The modern Eagle Rock Avenue / Prospect Avenue node lies about 10 m from the drawn junction and was left out of the fit; the drawn junction is the fire alarm box at the foot of the sheet.
Sheet is turned about 57 degrees (north toward the upper right), fitted from only three or four junctions on Eagle Rock Avenue.
West Orange, 200 ft; Eagle Rock Av strip with Henry St, Terrace Av, Forest Rd (today Forest Avenue); hand-picked points, low

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8, at 200 feet to an inch, shows the Eagle Rock Terrace tract in West Orange between Pleasant Valley Way at the top and Prospect Avenue at the bottom. Eagle Rock Avenue enters at the upper left at the Pleasant Valley Way crossing, where there is a fire alarm box, and runs south, bends south-west and leaves the sheet at the lower left to meet Prospect Avenue. Pleasant Valley Way crosses the top of the sheet from left to right. Between them a grid of narrow 40 and 50 foot streets was laid out across former farm land: Ellis, Orly, Cannon, Nicholas Avenue, Woodland Avenue, Pearl and Harper run north-south, crossed by Forest Avenue, Eagle, Redwood Avenue, Henry and Terrace Avenue. Most of the long lots are still vacant and none are built on. North of the tract the farms of Fred Schrump, Jennie B. Mayers, Chas. Fentzlaff, Louis Green, Robert Hopkins, Isabella Hopkins and Catherine Hopkins run down from Pleasant Valley Way, and Julia Williams holds the wedge beside Eagle Rock Avenue. The Augusta Munn Tilney estate with its house and outbuildings fills the lower left, and a farm group stands at the right edge. Eagle Rock Reservation occupies the foot of the sheet around Prospect Avenue. Streets are lettered with their widths, and the elevation of the roads is shown in circles. The compass rose is turned about 55 degrees, with north toward the upper right.
notes: Cannon is drawn as a straight street; the modern Cannon Street is curved and was left out of the fit, as was Henry Street.
Eagle, Orly and Pearl are not in OpenStreetMap; Forest Avenue, Redwood Avenue, Nicholas Avenue, Woodland Avenue, Harper Street and Ellis Street survive under these names.
The fitted scale is about 1.95 px/ft, 2 percent under the atlas value, and the south-west strip along Eagle Rock Avenue sits tens of metres from the modern street in the fit.
West Orange, 200 ft; Eagle Rock Av, Prospect Av, Eagle Rock Reservation; medium-low

sheet-9-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 9 is the upper two thirds of the sheet, drawn at 200 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the upper right. It shows the northern end of Pleasant Valley Way in the far north of West Orange, which runs along the bottom of the part, up to the line of the Borough of Verona, drawn as a dash-dot line crossing the road near the right edge. The area is open country divided into long, narrow farm and estate holdings running back from Pleasant Valley Way, each lettered with its owner: Jos. Weisbecker, Charlotte Hopkins, Isaac M. Ward, Robert Hopkins, Annie E. Kerling, Catherine E. Maynard, Jacob Frederick, Floyd Maynard, Jas. Jennings, W. E. Condit, J. F. Burns, Geo. D. Randall Est. and Charles H. Gardes, with the large Mary E. Wilde holding and smaller lots behind them. Buildings are few: small frame dwellings, barns and coops close to the road. No cross street meets Pleasant Valley Way on this part. A water pipe and hydrant are marked at the west end of the road. Sheet 4 adjoins at the left and sheet 10 below Pleasant Valley Way; a heavy line separates this part from part 2, a 100 ft to an inch view of Prospect Avenue drawn on the lower third of the same sheet.
notes: Placed from one hand-picked point only: Pleasant Valley Way at the Verona line, which is today where Pleasant Valley Way becomes Lakeside Avenue; scale (1.99 px/ft) and rotation are assumed from the atlas and from part 2.
Owners' names along Pleasant Valley Way: Weisbecker, Hopkins, Ward, Kerling, Maynard, Frederick, Jennings, Condit, Burns, Randall, Gardes, Wilde.

West Orange; two parts: part 1 (top) 200 ft to an inch, Pleasant Valley Way north of sheet 10, Borough of Verona line; part 2 (bottom) 100 ft to an inch, Prospect Av / Mt Pleasant Av / Ridge Road, separated by a heavy line

sheet-9-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 9 is the lower third of the sheet, below a heavy dividing line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the upper right. It shows a strip of estate land on the First Mountain in West Orange between Prospect Avenue along the top and Ridge Road along the bottom, ending at Mount Pleasant Avenue at the right edge, where a fire alarm box stands at the corner of Prospect Avenue and a water pipe runs along Prospect Avenue. The land is divided into large lots running from road to road, lettered with their owners: George V. Hecker Est., Mrs. Francis Hartley, Marcellus Hartley Est. and Treadwell Cleveland. Each holds a house with stables, coops and sheds set back in grounds; the largest group of buildings is on the Hecker estate. The beginning of Marcella Avenue is drawn just beyond Mount Pleasant Avenue at the right edge, continued on sheet 17. Large buildings at the left edge belong to sheet 29, and sheet 27 adjoins below Ridge Road. The upper two thirds of the sheet is part 1, a 200 ft to an inch view of Pleasant Valley Way.
notes: Placed from two junctions only (Mount Pleasant Avenue at Prospect Avenue and at Ridge Road): a helmert fit, low confidence.
Marcella Avenue as drawn leaves Mount Pleasant Avenue; today Marcella Avenue meets Prospect Avenue further north-east.

West Orange; two parts: part 1 (top) 200 ft to an inch, Pleasant Valley Way north of sheet 10, Borough of Verona line; part 2 (bottom) 100 ft to an inch, Prospect Av / Mt Pleasant Av / Ridge Road, separated by a heavy line

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10, at 200 feet to an inch, shows the north-eastern edge of West Orange against the Verona boundary. Pleasant Valley Way crosses the top of the sheet from the left edge and bends upward to the right edge. Prospect Avenue runs along the foot of the sheet, and Eagle Rock Reservation is named below it. The Borough of Verona boundary is a dash-dot line running down the right side of the sheet. Harper, Forest Avenue and Redwood Avenue, the last streets of the Eagle Rock Terrace tract continued from sheet 8, appear at the left edge. The remainder of the sheet is drawn as long narrow farm lots running from Pleasant Valley Way toward Prospect Avenue, labelled with their owners, among them Jos. Weisbecker, L. Green, Robert Hopkins, Isaac M. Ward, Annie Kerling, Lizzie B. Neiderbreit, Geo. Randall, Chas. H. Gardes, Alfred J. Crane, Peter Dern, Eliza A. Enderlin, Benj. F. Ilgen, Julia H. Susman and Henry N. Bowers. Two long lots at the right belong to the Montclair Golf Club. Buildings are few: small groups stand along Pleasant Valley Way, on the Bowers lot at lower left and beside Prospect Avenue, and a cluster of outbuildings sits on the Golf Club land. The compass rose at the top is turned about 55 degrees, so north lies toward the upper right.
notes: Anchored on the Harper Street / Redwood Avenue junction with the scale taken from neighbouring sheet 8; only one junction is measured, so placement is low confidence.
Forest Avenue / Harper Street was left out of the fit because the modern nodes are about 5 percent farther apart than the drawn ones.
West Orange, 200 ft; Pleasant Valley Way to Prospect, Harper, Redwood; Verona line; anchored, low

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11, at 200 feet to an inch, shows the south-western part of West Orange around Saint Cloud Avenue, Fairview Avenue and Northfield Avenue. Saint Cloud Avenue runs up the left side of the sheet from Northfield Avenue at the lower left corner to the top, with a stream (unnamed) beside it on the west. Mountain Avenue leaves the top, bends east and meets Ridgeway Avenue at the right edge, where a fire alarm box stands. Ridgeway Avenue then runs down the right side past Ivy Avenue, Benvenue Avenue and Fairview Avenue to Northfield Avenue, where Cable Road and Ridgeway Road diverge at the lower right. Fairview Avenue crosses the sheet from Saint Cloud Avenue to Ridgeway Avenue through the Llewellyn Realty Co. land. Edgewood Avenue and Highland Boulevard are laid out as streets off it. The ground is mostly large estates and farms, among them Wm B. Pierson, Daniel S. Baldwin Est., Joel Van Cise, Josephine M. Schweinler, Abraham Kleinberg, John Dane Jr., John Meirhoffer Est., R. H. Martin and M. P. Bower. Several houses stand in a row on the south side of Fairview Avenue near Ridgeway Avenue, and Saint Cloud School stands at the lower left. Walker Road and Mosswood Avenue enter from the south. The compass rose at upper right is turned only slightly, with north nearly at the top.
notes: The street printed Mountain Avenue between Saint Cloud Avenue and Ridgeway Avenue is today's Old Indian Road.
Fairview Avenue / Highland Boulevard was left out: the modern node is about 19 m from the drawn junction.
Cable Road and the Ridgeway Road south of Northfield Avenue are not in OpenStreetMap.
Saint Cloud is printed St. Cloud.
West Orange, 200 ft; Saint Cloud, Mountain Av (today Old Indian Road), Ridgeway, Northfield; medium

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12, at 100 feet to an inch, is turned about 80 degrees so that north lies toward the right. It shows the Cable Lake district south of Northfield Avenue in West Orange. Northfield Avenue runs from the Walker Road junction at the top across to a circle marked 550 at the right edge, where Ridgeway Avenue and Cable Road meet it. Woodland Boulevard runs diagonally across the left side to the Cable Road power house area at the bottom, crossed by Fairfield Avenue, Wildwood Avenue, Sunset Avenue, Ridgeway Avenue and Hawthorne Avenue. Mosswood Avenue crosses Ridgeway Avenue on the right. Most of the streets are laid out in a subdivision with lots lettered 160B to 160M and few buildings. Cable Lake lies at lower left beside Hawthorne Avenue with a boat house on the shore. Summit Drive curves along the foot of the sheet. At the lower right is the Cable Road Power House, marked not used, with a small adjoining building. A waiting room stands at the Walker Road end of Northfield Avenue, and Mrs. R. M. L. Bonnet owns the large tract beside Northfield Avenue. A dashed line beside Northfield Avenue marks a water pipe. A bar scale in the lower right corner gives 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Only two junctions survive in OpenStreetMap (Northfield Avenue with Walker Road and with Ridgeway Avenue); the part is a two-point helmert and low confidence.
The fitted scale (3.78 px/ft) is about 4 percent below the neighbouring sheets, and the drawn distance between the two junctions is shorter than the modern one.
Fairfield Avenue, Woodland Boulevard, Cable Road and Summit Drive are not in OpenStreetMap.
West Orange, 100 ft, turned about 81 degrees; Walker Rd, Northfield, Mosswood, Cable Lake; two-point helmert, low

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13, at 100 feet to an inch, shows Crystal Lake and the grounds of English's Crystal Lake Park Hotel in West Orange. Prospect Avenue crosses the top of the sheet from the left edge, curving toward the right, to its junction with Eagle Rock Avenue near the upper right corner, marked with a fire alarm box. Eagle Rock Avenue runs south along the right edge, bending to the south-east and leaving at the right edge, and is named along its length as bordering Eagle Rock Reservation. Crystal Lake fills the middle of the sheet. On its east shore stand the hotel and its outbuildings, including a carousel and sheds, on the John English property. West of the lake the land is held by John English, and the lower left belongs to Mrs. H. T. Shriver, whose house, sheds and a garage stand in a clearing, with Julia Williams to the east of it. Rocky Way, a private road of the Llewellyn Park district, runs along the foot of the sheet with a curve at the left. Water pipe follows Prospect Avenue and Eagle Rock Avenue. The compass rose at upper right is turned about 70 degrees, with north toward the upper right.
notes: Anchored on the Eagle Rock Avenue / Prospect Avenue junction with scale and rotation from neighbours; low confidence.
Rocky Way is a private road of the Llewellyn Park district; its junction with Mountain Avenue lies off this sheet.
West Orange, 100 ft; Prospect Av, Eagle Rock Av, Crystal Lake; anchored on Eagle Rock / Prospect, low

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 covers the thinly built northern edge of West Orange, at 100 feet to an inch, with the sheet turned about 30 degrees counterclockwise so that Eagle Rock Avenue and Mountain Avenue run roughly down the page. Eagle Rock Avenue enters from the top and from the upper left in two branches that join and run south-east to meet Mountain Avenue at the right edge of the sheet; Mountain Avenue then continues down the right edge to Rocky Way, a 50-foot street which leaves it near the bottom and bends away to the south-west, with a second short stretch of Rocky Way running on from the foot of the sheet. Almost all of the sheet is unsubdivided land lettered with owners' names: Ellis C. Beale Est. across the west, Amanda F. Green and A. Heald Est. toward the east and south, with block numbers 109 and 110. The only built-up group is at the top, around an estate lettered Wildmont, where several dwellings and sheds are marked dilapidated, and near the Eagle Rock Quarry Co., whose note gives its power, heat and light. A few dwellings stand beside Eagle Rock Avenue and Mountain Avenue. The Eagle Rock Reservation is lettered along the upper left. Water pipes run in Eagle Rock Avenue and Mountain Avenue, and hydrant and fire alarm marks occur along them. Neighbouring sheets are 13, 18, 21 and 16.
notes: Eagle Rock Avenue and Mountain Avenue meet at a four-way junction that OpenStreetMap carries as two nodes 29 m apart; the control point is hand-picked at their midpoint.
The part has no street junction that the detector can measure except Mountain Avenue / Rocky Way; the placement rests on two points.
Owner names read at full resolution: Ellis C. Beale Est., A. Heald Est., Amanda F. Green (initial read as F, medium confidence).
West Orange, 100 ft; north edge at Eagle Rock / Mountain / Rocky Way, estates; helmert, low

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 lies in the western part of West Orange, at 100 feet to an inch, turned about 25 degrees counterclockwise so that Prospect Avenue runs down the left edge. The sheet shows large undivided parcels with almost no streets. Prospect Avenue, with a 60-foot width and water pipe, is the only public street, drawn along the left edge from the top to the bottom. On the right, The Ramble, a private road of Llewellyn Park, runs down the right edge from the middle of the sheet to the bottom. A right of way lettered as such crosses the lower part of the sheet from Prospect Avenue up to The Ramble. The land is lettered with owners: Emily Lawrence at the top, Thomas B. Blackburn Est. and Charles A. Munn in the middle, Caroline E. Harrison, Rebecca Tilley and Wm. R. Howe along Prospect Avenue, and Dudley Farrand to the south-east, with block numbers 105 and 106. The only buildings are a small group of dwellings and outbuildings on the Howe land beside Prospect Avenue. The north arrow is at the top. Neighbouring sheets are 13 above, 7 and 6 at the left, 16 at the right and 17 below.
notes: The sheet has no street junction of its own. It is placed by control points carried from sheet 17, which repeats the right-of-way lines and the corner at Prospect Avenue; it needs sheet 17 placed first.
Owner names read at medium confidence on the overview-scale crop for Caroline E. Harrison and Rebecca Tilley; others read at full resolution.
The Ramble is private and is not in OpenStreetMap.
West Orange, 100 ft; estates on Prospect Av and The Ramble, no junction; anchored with points carried from sheet 17, low

sheet-16-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 16 is the right half of the sheet, east of a heavy vertical dividing line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It shows estate grounds in the upper part of Llewellyn Park, the private residential park on the slope of the First Mountain in West Orange. Rocky Way winds across the top of the part from the edge of sheet 13 to Mountain Avenue, which curves down the right side of the part past Lynwood Way and Park Way toward sheet 23. The Ramble, one of the park's drives, runs down the left side along the dividing line, with a right of way leaving it near the bottom. Between these roads lie a few very large holdings: the D. A. Heald Est. in the upper left, the H. Parrish Jr. house with its stable and outbuildings near Rocky Way, the Charles A. Munn grounds with the large frame mansion called The Terraces and a cluster of outbuildings, and land of the Orange Savings Bank at the bottom. Most of the part is open ground. A water pipe and hydrants are marked along Mountain Avenue. The left half of the sheet, west of the dividing line, is part 2.
notes: Placed from one junction only, Mountain Avenue / Rocky Way, with the atlas scale (3.98 px/ft) and rotation from the lines measured there: low confidence.

Lynwood Way and Park Way meet Mountain Avenue about 90 m apart on the sheet but 23 m apart in OpenStreetMap, and the distances from Rocky Way do not agree with the sheet scale: the Llewellyn Park drives have been realigned or are mapped differently today; they were not used.
The Ramble is not in the OpenStreetMap street data.
The Terraces, the house of Charles A. Munn.

West Orange, 100 ft; two parts side by side split by a heavy vertical line: part 1 (left) The Ramble, Tulip Av, Cliff Rd, Mt Pleasant Av (Llewellyn Park); part 2 (right) The Ramble, Mountain Av, Rocky Way

sheet-16-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 16 is the left half of the sheet, west of a heavy vertical dividing line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It shows the western part of Llewellyn Park in West Orange, the private residential park on the slope of the First Mountain. The Ramble runs down the left side of the part, Mountain Avenue curves across the upper right to meet Tulip Avenue, and Tulip Avenue winds down the middle of the part in tight bends to Mount Pleasant Avenue at the bottom. Cliff Road loops between The Ramble and Mount Pleasant Avenue, and a second stretch of The Ramble crosses the part between Mountain Avenue and its western branch. The land is laid out as large, unbuilt lots lettered with their owners: N. H. Chesbrough, Chas. Kocher, A. H. B. Howe, the Llewellyn Park Improvement Co. and Amos Binney. No buildings are drawn on this part. Water pipes and hydrants are marked on Mountain Avenue and Mount Pleasant Avenue. Sheets 15 and 17 adjoin on the left and sheet 27 below. The right half of the sheet, east of the dividing line, is part 1.
notes: Placed from one hand-picked junction only, Mountain Avenue / Tulip Avenue, with the atlas scale (3.98 px/ft) and the rotation of part 1: low confidence.
Today Tulip Avenue does not continue down to Mount Pleasant Avenue as drawn; The Ramble and Cliff Road are not in the OpenStreetMap street data.

West Orange, 100 ft; two parts side by side split by a heavy vertical line: part 1 (left) The Ramble, Tulip Av, Cliff Rd, Mt Pleasant Av (Llewellyn Park); part 2 (right) The Ramble, Mountain Av, Rocky Way

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 shows the south-west corner of the Llewellyn Park district of West Orange, at 100 feet to an inch, turned about 25 degrees counterclockwise. Prospect Avenue runs down the left side of the sheet from the top to the Mount Pleasant Avenue crossing at the bottom left, with a water pipe in it. Mount Pleasant Avenue runs along the bottom, east from Prospect Avenue, and ends on the right at a fork with Tulip Avenue. Cliff Road climbs the right side from Mount Pleasant Avenue to The Ramble, which comes down the upper right, and a right of way runs across the top to The Ramble. The upper two thirds is large undivided parcels lettered with owners: Mitchell Bros., G. H. McFadden, G. V. Hecker Est., J. L. Hardy, Walton C. Whittingham, John W. Wilmer and M. Hartley Est. Dwellings, hotels (one lettered H. Koch Hotel) and sheds line Prospect Avenue below. The built-up part is at the bottom, around Marcella Avenue and the platted lots of block 83 near Prospect Avenue and Mount Pleasant Avenue, with an iron reservoir beside Marcella Avenue, D. Fusco's Quarry, and E. Cowan's premises with a factory and dwellings on the lots between Mount Pleasant Avenue and Cliff Road. Ridge Road leaves Mount Pleasant Avenue at the bottom. The sheet number 17 is at top left, with neighbouring sheets 15, 6, 16, 9 and 27.
notes: The part is anchored on one measured point (Prospect Avenue / Mount Pleasant Avenue) with the atlas scale and a rotation of -24.4 degrees from Prospect Avenue; low confidence.
Marcella Avenue / Prospect Avenue was left out: the OpenStreetMap node is about 10 percent short of the drawn distance from Mount Pleasant Avenue.
Owner names Walton C. Whittingham and John W. Wilmer read at overview scale, medium confidence; the rest read at full resolution.
West Orange, 100 ft; Prospect / Mount Pleasant / Marcella, Cliff Road; anchored, low

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 covers the north-east part of West Orange along Mountain Avenue and Valley Way, at 100 feet to an inch, turned about 47 degrees clockwise. Eagle Rock Avenue comes down the left edge from the top and meets Mountain Avenue at the left; Mountain Avenue runs north-east across the upper half to the right edge. Valley Way runs along the bottom, from the lower left to the right edge. Between them an unevenly platted district is laid out with Nutwold Avenue (80 feet), Murray, a street lettered Proposed, and Matthew, Benjamin and Amos, which run down to Valley Way; Wilfred Street leaves Valley Way at the bottom. Parkside Place and Parkside Avenue join Valley Way at the lower left. The north-east corner is cut by the line of the Town of Montclair, and the City View Hotel stands at the Mountain Avenue corner. Most blocks (148A, 148B, 149) are large and unbuilt, with dwellings concentrated along Valley Way, around Amos and Matthew, and on the Phoebe M. Dunning estate to the west. Eagle Rock Reservation is lettered across the top of the sheet, north of Mountain Avenue. A north arrow and the scale bar are at the lower right. The sheet joins sheets 14 (above), 21 (left) and 19 (below).
notes: Eagle Rock Avenue / Mountain Avenue is a four-way junction of two OpenStreetMap nodes 29 m apart; the control point is hand-picked at their midpoint, the same point as on sheet 14. The detector's pick for it sat 260 px (65 ft) off and was excluded.

Matthew, Benjamin and Amos carry no printed suffix on this sheet (sheet 19 prints Matthew St., Benjamin St., Amos St.). Modern Amos Street and Matthew Street exist; Benjamin Street is not in OpenStreetMap.
Street names read from overview-scale crops except those at the control points; medium confidence.
West Orange, 100 ft; Mountain Av / Valley Way district at the Montclair line; medium

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 covers the Valley Way district of West Orange, at 100 feet to an inch, turned about 55 degrees clockwise so that Valley Way runs diagonally from the lower left to the upper right. Eagle Rock Avenue runs up the left side from Bloomfield Way, and the stream drawn in blue crosses the sheet from upper right to lower left. The streets platted between Valley Way and Harrison Avenue include Parkside Place and Parkside Avenue, Elm, Chestnut and Mississippi Avenue, Maple, and Wilfred, with Benjamin Street, Matthew Street and Amos Street running off to the north of Valley Way. Harrison Avenue crosses the bottom, where Cherry Street, Chestnut Street, Elm Street and Maple Street join it. In the east, blocks 140A and 140B are large lots crossed by streets lettered Not Named, with Wilfred Street, Warman Street and Virginia Avenue near the bottom right. Dwellings fill the lots along Valley Way, Parkside Place, Elm and Maple, and the blocks west of the stream (142 to 147) are mostly built. The boundary of the Town of Montclair runs up the right side. Llewellyn Park Drive and Bloomfield Way are lettered at the left edge, and a north arrow and scale bar fill the top and bottom. Neighbouring sheets are 18, 20, 21 and 22.
notes: Control rests on the Valley Way junctions with Wilfred Street, Parkside Avenue and Eagle Rock Avenue / Bloomfield Way (the drawn junction at the left, about 160 m from Elm Street, not the lower junction numbered 22).
Several streets east of Wilfred carry the label Not Named and are not listed.
Street names read from overview-scale crops except those near the bottom edge; medium confidence for Kirk Street and Warman Street.
West Orange, 100 ft; Valley Way / Harrison Av district; good

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 covers a residential district of West Orange between Harrison Avenue on the west and Franklin Avenue on the east, from the Town of Montclair boundary at the top of the sheet down to Eagle Rock Avenue and the brook at the bottom. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that Harrison Avenue runs up the page. Between the two avenues a regular series of narrow east-west streets (Kirk, Maple, Elm, Chestnut and Cherry) cut the area into long blocks numbered 135 to 139, lined with frame dwellings on narrow lots, with small houses and open lots toward Franklin Avenue. Oxford Place, Orange Place and Ashwood Terrace run off Cherry Street toward the south, where larger open blocks, one marked 125B and with proposed streets drawn in outline, hold a few scattered houses. A brook crosses the lower part of the sheet from the left edge to the right, passing under Eagle Rock Avenue, which runs diagonally along the bottom. At the lower right Seward Street, Ridge Avenue and William Street form a built-up block of small houses with numbered lots, and Holy Trinity Episcopal Church with a church house stands beside the brook near William Street. Water pipes with their diameters, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked along the streets. The blank areas at the right and top belong to sheets 60 and 57 of the series, and the blank strip beyond Harrison Avenue to sheet 19.
notes: Eagle Rock Avenue along the bottom of the sheet is today Main Street in the modern street data (Eagle Rock Avenue now begins further north).
The Main Street / Park Terrace and Main Street / William Street nodes lie about 25 m apart in the modern data and were left out of the fit; the sheet draws one junction there.
The streets drawn as proposed (south of Cherry Street, block 125B) are not in the modern street data.
Bishop, Randall Avenue and Randall Terrace are not in the modern street data under those names.
West Orange, 100 ft; Harrison / Franklin Av blocks, Eagle Rock Av (today Main Street) along the bottom; high

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 shows the Llewellyn Park district of West Orange, at 100 feet to an inch, turned about 35 degrees clockwise. Mountain Avenue crosses the upper part from the left edge to the upper right, where Rocky Way leaves it to the north and Long Branch turns south from it. Long Branch winds down the middle of the sheet, with a water pipe in it, and joins Lynwood Way, which runs from the upper left corner to the lower middle; at the junction the road continues south-east as Bloomfield Way, which also runs down the right half of the sheet toward the corner and meets a branch lettered Bloomfield Way at the lower left. Eagle Rock Avenue runs down the right edge beside a stream, and Llewellyn Park Drive branches from Bloomfield Way at the lower right. The land is large private estates: C. D. Cleveland (Sunnybrook), H. Barry (Barrymead), W. Wallace, B. D. Whiting, Annie Gillespie and Mrs. T. Williams, with blocks numbered 103 and 112. Dwellings and outbuildings stand on each estate, one shown in a pink wash for its brick or stone. A brook crosses the western parcel. The sheet joins sheets 14 above, 16 and 23 at the left, 22 below and 18 and 19 at the right.
notes: The part is anchored on Mountain Avenue / Rocky Way (the junction also drawn on sheet 14 and 16-1) with the atlas scale; low confidence.

The drawn Long Branch and the OpenStreetMap Long Branch Way follow different alignments by up to about 55 m, and Lynwood Way / Long Branch Way and Mountain Avenue near Lynwood Way sit 28 to 45 m off the drawn positions, so they were not used.
Owner names read from overview-scale crops, medium confidence.
West Orange, 100 ft; Llewellyn Park (Mountain Av, Long Branch, Lynwood Way); anchored on Mountain / Rocky Way, low

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 shows the western edge of the Llewellyn Park district of West Orange and the lower end of Eagle Rock Avenue. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about a quarter turn, so that Eagle Rock Avenue runs from the right of the sheet to the lower left corner. Bloomfield Way sweeps in a broad loop along the top and right of the sheet, joined by Glen Avenue and Winding Way from the left, and by the private Llewellyn Park Drive on the right, enclosing a large undivided tract that holds a few scattered dwellings and outbuildings, including the property of E. A. Bredt. In the middle of the sheet Park Terrace runs north from Eagle Rock Avenue with a long row of small frame houses on narrow lots on its west side, and Randall Terrace and Randall Avenue form a loop around block 113A, mostly vacant lots laid out in rows. At the lower left Llewellyn Avenue, Ridgehurst Road and McKinley Place run north from Eagle Rock Avenue and form the closely built part of the sheet, with frame dwellings on narrow lots along block 113B. Ashwood Terrace and a proposed street leave Eagle Rock Avenue on its south side. At the right, Mississippi Avenue and Harrison Avenue meet Eagle Rock Avenue at a fire alarm box. Water pipes with diameters, hydrants and street lamp numbers are marked. The blank areas belong to adjoining sheets 19, 20, 21, 23 and 24.
notes: Eagle Rock Avenue along the lower part of the sheet is today Main Street in the modern street data.
McKinley Place appears to be today's McKinley Avenue where it meets Main Street.
Glen Avenue and Bloomfield Way meet at the top of the sheet as they do today.
Randall, Randall Terrace, Randall Avenue, Winding Way, Linwood Way and Llewellyn Park Drive are private Llewellyn Park roads and are not in the modern street data under these names.
The modern Bloomfield Way / Eagle Rock Avenue / Valley Way junction at the right edge lies about 8 m off its drawn position relative to the other control and was left out of the fit.
West Orange, 100 ft, turned (north to the right); Llewellyn Park west edge, Eagle Rock Av (today Main Street); medium

sheet-23.description: Sheet 23 shows the central part of Llewellyn Park, the private residential park in West Orange, at 100 feet to an inch. Mountain Avenue forms the west side of the sheet and bends down to meet Tulip Avenue at the lower left. The park's winding private roads cut the land into large estates: Lynwood Way runs east from Mountain Avenue along the top of the sheet, Park Way and Oak Bend loop around the middle, and Glen Avenue and Bloomfield Way run along the east side, with Honeysuckle Avenue leaving the lower right corner. The blocks, numbered 98, 100, 101 and 102, hold a few large houses with lodges, greenhouses and stables set in open grounds, named for their owners on the sheet: Mrs Henry N. Munn, Edith Hyde Colby (with Oldstead Lodge), A. B. Jenkins (with the greenhouses and Chestnut Hall), Anna G. Jenkins, Agnes I. Vincent, Geo. Merck, J. M. McKim estate, and the house Oakleigh on block 101. A brook runs diagonally across the lower left, and the large area at the left, enclosed by the loop of Mountain Avenue, is marked The Ramble. Water pipes, hydrants and the numbers of the street lamps are marked along the roads, and house outlines are drawn in yellow, pink and blue by construction. The blank margins belong to adjoining sheets 16, 21, 22, 24, 25 and 26.
notes: Lynwood Way, Oak Bend, Park Way and Long Branch are private Llewellyn Park roads whose lines in the modern street data do not match the sheet; the Oak Bend and Park Way nodes lie 10 to 15 m from the sheet's lines and were left out of the control.
The fit rests on three junctions (Mountain Avenue with Tulip Avenue and with Lynwood Way, and Bloomfield Way with Glen Avenue), so it is an exact fit with no redundancy.
Bloomfield Way and Glen Avenue join at the right edge as they do today.
West Orange, 100 ft; Llewellyn Park (Lynwood Way, Oak Bend, Park Way); three-point exact fit, low

sheet-24.description: Sheet 24 covers the southern part of Llewellyn Park in West Orange, from Glen Avenue and Park Way at the top down to Valley and Eagle Rock Avenue along the bottom, at 100 feet to an inch. The sheet is turned so that the bottom edge runs roughly east to west. Honeysuckle Avenue runs down the left side, Glen Avenue crosses the middle and curves up along the east side past Winding Way, and Llewellyn Avenue forms the right edge. The upper half is made up of large private estates in open grounds, block 101, with houses, greenhouses and stables named for their owners on the sheet: D. F. Cox, Thomas A. Edison, Beatrice Nichols Douglass, Bertha Mitchell Nichols, Elizabeth W. Burke (with the house Wood Lands) and the house Elm Court. South of Glen Avenue lie more estates, among them Bonaire, Blythewood, G. Richards, T. N. Foster and C. F. Smith, and the large block 114. Near the bottom edge the land is divided into narrow building lots along Edisonia Terrace, Prospect Place and Llewellyn Avenue, with small frame dwellings and, along Valley, a few shops and a wagon works. Alden Street, Babcock Place, Kling Street and Lakeside Avenue enter from the south side of Valley. Hydrants, water pipes with diameters and street lamp numbers are marked. The blank margins belong to adjoining sheets 22, 23, 26, 52, 53, 55 and 57.
notes: Valley along the bottom of the sheet is today Main Street in the modern street data.
Edge Hill Avenue is today Edgehill Avenue.
Park Way, Winding Way and the roads inside Llewellyn Park are private; only Glen Avenue and Honeysuckle Avenue were used as control and agree with the Main Street junctions.
West Orange, 100 ft; Llewellyn Park south and Valley (today Main Street); high

sheet-25.description: Sheet 25 shows the western part of Llewellyn Park in West Orange at 100 feet to an inch, with the sheet turned so that its top edge faces roughly north-west. Mountain Avenue crosses the sheet from the left, where Gregory Avenue enters from the west, to its junction with Tulip Avenue at the right. Wildwood Avenue continues from Mountain Avenue down the left side, and Tulip Avenue runs from Mount Pleasant Avenue and Cliff Road at the top in a series of sharp bends, then down the right side of the sheet to Oak Bend and Park Way at the bottom. Almost the whole area is large estate grounds with a few houses, lodges and outbuildings, named for their owners on the sheet: Mary G. Goodrich, Sarah R. Martin, Emily M. Dixon (block 85A), the Llewellyn Park Improvement Co., A. B. Malcomson, Henry D. Newson (with the house Castlewood), Blythe Lea, Broad Acres, D. E. Green Jr. (Beech Lodge), David E. Green Est. (block 97) and Geo. J. Seabury (Sunny Side). A small brook rises beside Mountain Avenue near Gregory Avenue and runs south-west. Water pipes with their diameters, hydrants and street lamp numbers are marked along the public roads. Trefoil Pass enters Oak Bend at the bottom edge. The blank margins belong to the adjoining sheets 16, 23, 26, 27 and 28.
notes: Cliff Road is not in the modern street data.
Mount Pleasant Avenue at the top of the sheet and Tulip Avenue north of Mountain Avenue were not matched to the modern street data and were not used.

The part is placed from one junction (Mountain Avenue with Tulip Avenue) at the scale of its neighbours and a rotation measured from the drawn lines at that junction (62.7 degrees), which agrees with the sheet's north arrow; it is low confidence. A second junction, Mountain Avenue / Oak Bend Road / Wildwood Avenue, would give a 3 percent larger scale and was left out as displaced in the modern data.
The modern Oak Bend Road nodes at Trefoil Pass, Tulip Avenue and Park Way lie 7 to 13 m from the drawn lines and were not used.
West Orange, 100 ft; Llewellyn Park west; anchored on Mountain / Tulip, low

sheet-26.description: Sheet 26 shows the south-western part of Llewellyn Park in West Orange at 100 feet to an inch, with the sheet turned so that its top edge faces roughly north-west. Two winding private roads, Tulip Avenue and Park Way, run down the sheet in long curves on either side of a brook that crosses the sheet from top to bottom, with the roadway between them lettered The Ramble. Glen Avenue crosses the sheet from the junction with Park Way to Honeysuckle Avenue on the right, and Edge Hill Avenue runs along the bottom and turns up beside the estates at the lower right. Trefoil Pass and Forest Way enter from the left near the top. Almost all of the land is held in large estates with a few houses and outbuildings, named on the sheet: David E. Green Est. (block 96), Emma S. Cole, Thomas A. Edison (block 91, with the house Glenmont, which stands near Honeysuckle Avenue), R. C. Browning Est. (block 92), A. C. Wall (block 90), Margaret A. Colgate (Hollyoaks), H. B. Ruchincloss, Grace E. Quimby, J. Miller Est., Bertha Greenleaf and G. H. Sedgwick (block 89). Water pipes, hydrants and street lamp numbers are marked along the roads. The left half of the sheet is blank paper belonging to sheets 28 and 51, and the lower right corner is shared with sheets 24 and 52.
notes: The Ramble is lettered along the roadway between Tulip Avenue and Park Way, and as an area name on the neighbouring sheets 16 and 23.
Wildwood Way at the lower left is today Wildwood Avenue.
Edge Hill Avenue is today Edgehill Avenue.

The part is placed from one junction (Glen Avenue with Honeysuckle Avenue, also drawn on sheet 24) at the scale of its neighbours, with rotation measured from the drawn lines at that junction (59.9 degrees); it is low confidence. The Park Way, Edgehill Avenue and Tulip Avenue nodes of the modern street data disagreed with this by 5 to 30 m and were not used.
Llewellyn Park roads are private and have no surrounding parcels in the modern parcel data.
West Orange, 100 ft; Llewellyn Park south-west; anchored on Glen / Honeysuckle, low

sheet-27.description: Sheet 27 covers the north-western part of West Orange, a district of large country estates, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Ridge Road crosses the top of the sheet from left to right and ends at Mt. Pleasant Av., which runs down the upper right corner, bends south-west at a 60 foot street and then runs as a straight diagonal across the whole sheet to the lower left. There it meets Gregory Av., which comes in from the left and also runs east across the lower part of the sheet to the junction with Mountain Av. and Wildwood Av. at the right edge. Below that junction Mt. Pleasant Av. continues down the lower left corner. Nearly all the ground is open land held by named owners: Geo. V. Hecker Est., H. K. White, The Hartley Est., L. F. Loree and Treadwell Cleveland along Ridge Road, the large Daniel O'Rourke Quarry Co. plot in the middle with its quarry buildings, John W. Wilmer, Sarah C. Whittingham and Eliza C. Wilmer to the east of the quarry, and the Essex County Country Club between Gregory Av. and the diagonal. A winding stream with a blue outline runs down the left side, and two private roads cross the left half. Buildings are few, mostly frame dwellings, outbuildings and sheds, with one stone house near the Hecker estate. Water pipes and hydrants are marked on Mt. Pleasant Av. and Gregory Av. Neighbouring sheets named in the margins are 9 above, 29 and 30 on the left, 17 and 16 on the right, 25 at the lower right and 28 below.
notes: Mount Pleasant Av. is Mount Pleasant Avenue today; the diagonal reach between Gregory Av. and the bend near the top right follows the modern road.

The east leg of Gregory Av. as far as the Mountain Av. and Wildwood Av. junction follows today's Gregory Avenue and Mount Pleasant Avenue only in part; that junction has no counterpart in the modern street data.
Placed from only two control points (Mount Pleasant Avenue / Ridge Road and the north node of Gregory Avenue / Mount Pleasant Avenue); low confidence.
West Orange, 100 ft; Mount Pleasant Av between Ridge Rd and Gregory Av, estates; helmert, low

sheet-28.description: Sheet 28 shows the Llewellyn Park side of the Mount Pleasant district of West Orange, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Mt. Pleasant Av. runs down the left edge of the sheet, with Mt. Pleasant Pl., Mountain View Av., Longview Av., Park Pl. and Gaston St. entering from the left. Wildwood Av. leaves the upper part of the sheet, curves south-east past the Wm. Read Howe place, meets Oak Bend and Forest Way at the top and middle, and runs on south-west as Wildwood Way to Mt. Pleasant Av. at the bottom. Oak Bend curves east to Trefoil Pass, a 50 foot street running down the right side to Forest Way, and Tulip Av. curves south from the right edge to the bottom of the sheet. The blocks between the streets are large estates and holdings: R. Colgate (Oak Brook), W. D. Smith, H. Folsom, Salvatore Stizer and F. T. Browning, with the long Golf Land Co. of Essex Co. tract along Mt. Pleasant Av. A winding brook with blue outline crosses the sheet from top to bottom, and its course is followed by Wildwood Av. Buildings are scattered frame dwellings and stables, with a few pink brick or stone houses. Water pipes, hydrants and a fire alarm box are marked along Mt. Pleasant Av. Sheet numbers in the margins are 27, 25, 26, 31 and 51. The compass at the lower right points up and to the right.
notes: Oak Bend, Trefoil Pass, Forest Way and Tulip Av. survive as Oak Bend Road, Trefoil Pass, Forest Way and Tulip Avenue.
Wildwood Av. between Oak Bend and Forest Way survives as Wildwood Avenue; the Wildwood Way reach to Mt. Pleasant Av. at the bottom is not in the modern street data under that name.
Mountain View Av. is Mountain View Street today.

Placed from four detected junctions (Forest Way / Wildwood Avenue, Forest Way / Trefoil Pass, Oak Bend Road / Trefoil Pass, Tulip Avenue / Wildwood Avenue); the left strip with Mt. Pleasant Av. has no control of its own.
West Orange, 100 ft; Wildwood, Oak Bend, Trefoil Pass, Forest Way, Tulip; medium

sheet-29.description: Sheet 29 covers the western edge of the Llewellyn Park district of West Orange, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Prospect Av. runs down the left side from the top of the sheet to a bend near the bottom, where Mountain Av. leaves it to the west and Prospect Av. turns south-east. A second street, Ridge Rd., comes in from the top, turns at a right angle at the 30 foot Ridge Rd. crossing in the upper part and then runs south-east to the lower right, where it reaches Northfield Av. A Private Rd. runs down the right edge. The sheet is almost entirely large private estates, laid out as long strips between Prospect Av. and Ridge Rd.: Douglas Robinson (with his house Overlook), the estate of the Harding farm with its house The Homestead, Eugene Delano (Maywood), and Mary E. Brown with the houses Holmhurst and Brighthurst, together with their stables, greenhouses, cottages and summer houses. A compass at the left shows north pointing up and to the left. Water pipes are marked along Prospect Av. and Mountain Av. Neighbouring sheets named in the margins are 9, 27, 5, 30, 34 and 32. Most of the sheet is open lawn and field with only the estate buildings coloured, and there are no blocks of small lots.
notes: Prospect Av. is Prospect Avenue today and Ridge Rd. is Ridge Road; Mountain Av. at the bend matches Old Indian Road in the modern street data.

Placed from one detected junction (Old Indian Road / Prospect Avenue) at the configured 100 ft scale, with a derived second point; low confidence. The modern Prospect Avenue, Ridge Road and Northfield Avenue lines follow the drawn streets across the sheet.
West Orange, 100 ft; Prospect Av and Ridge Rd estates; anchored on Old Indian Road / Prospect, low

sheet-30.description: Sheet 30 lies between Northfield Av. on the left and Mt. Pleasant Av. on the right in West Orange, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Gregory Av. crosses the sheet from Northfield Av. at the left edge, is met by Hutton Av. coming down from the north and by a private road, then bends north-east and leaves at the right edge toward Mt. Pleasant Av. Linden Av. (Private Rd.) runs along the bottom from Northfield Av. to Hutton Av., and Hutton Av. runs down between the two. In the upper part Ridge Rd. and further private roads wind through the sheet toward the top right. A brook with a blue outline crosses the right half from the upper right to the lower left. The blocks are large rectangular holdings, many of them still vacant: H. S. Bishop Heirs at the top left, Lottie E. Mayer, F. Van Ness and D. F. Lingane north of Gregory Av., John C. Jacobson in the upper middle, W. D. Osborne south of Gregory Av., and the Essex County Country Club grounds at the lower right with a pavilion and club buildings. Neighbouring sheets named in the margins are 29, 34, 35, 27 and 31. The compass at the top shows north pointing up and to the right.
notes: Linden Av. (Private Rd.) and Gregory Av. survive as Linden Avenue and Gregory Avenue; the junction of Gregory Av. and Hutton Av. was matched to the modern Gregory Avenue / Linden Avenue node.
Mount Pleasant Av. at the right edge is Mount Pleasant Avenue today.
Placed from three detected junctions (an exact affine fit, no residual check); low to medium confidence.
West Orange, 100 ft; Gregory, Hutton, Linden (private road); three-point exact fit, low-medium

sheet-31.description: Sheet 31 shows the Mt. Pleasant Av. frontage of West Orange between the Essex County Country Club and Gaston, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Mt. Pleasant Av. runs down the right edge. Streets enter it from the left in a regular grid of long, narrow building lots: Mt. Pleasant Pl., Mountain View Av. and Long View Av., then Lindsley Av. and Condit Ter. running down from Long View Av. to Gaston at the bottom, with Wildwood Av. and Park Pl. at the lower right. The lots between the streets are numbered and most carry frame dwellings, with the houses closely set along Lindsley Av. and Condit Ter.; the upper blocks are mostly vacant. West of the grid lie the grounds of the Essex County Country Club, with a club house, a pavilion and a stone building in the middle, and a brook winding down the left centre. Along the top is a private road, and in the upper left are the estates of F. C. Reynolds, R. W. Parker and E. L. Newhouse behind Linden Av. (Private Rd.), with W. D. Sargent's place lower down and C. F. Rand's holdings in the upper right. Northfield Av. runs down the left edge and Rollinson St. enters it from the left. Neighbouring sheets named in the margins are 30, 35, 47, 49, 50, 51 and 28. The compass at the top points up and to the right.
notes: Mountain View Av. and Long View Av. are Mountain View Street and Longview Street today; Lindsley Av., Condit Ter. and Gaston are Lindsley Avenue, Condit Terrace and Gaston Street.
Mount Pleasant Pl. is not in the modern street data.
The street label at the bottom reads Gaston without a printed suffix on this sheet.
West Orange, 100 ft; Mount Pleasant Av lot grid (Mountain View, Long View, Lindsley, Condit Ter, Gaston); good

sheet-32.description: Sheet 32 covers the Ridgeway Av. and Northfield Av. district of West Orange south of Prospect Av., drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Prospect Av. comes in from the upper left and meets a curving road at the top; Benvenue Av. sweeps down from that junction in a wide arc to Ridgeway Av. at the left, with St. Cloud Pl. running parallel inside it. Ridgeway Av. runs down the left side and Mountain Av. crosses the top left. Northfield Av. runs diagonally from the lower left to the upper right and carries the heaviest building along its frontage; Hawthorne Av. branches east from it near the bottom, and Cable Road crosses the bottom edge. At the upper right Ridge Rd. comes down from the top. Between the streets are groups of lots with frame dwellings, the Mary E. Brown holding at the top, and the large tracts numbered 158, 158A and 158B. At the top left stand St. Cloud Presbyterian Church, its Sunday school and the St. Cloud Club House, and nearby the Church of the Holy Innocents. Water pipes and fire alarm boxes are marked along Ridgeway Av. and Northfield Av. Sheet numbers in the margins are 5, 29, 34, 33, 11 and 12. The compass at the left points up and to the left.
notes: Prospect Av., Benvenue Av., Ridgeway Av. and Northfield Av. survive under the same names; the modern Northfield Avenue is straighter than the drawn one.
The Cable Road label at the bottom has the sheet number 12 printed between ROAD and AV.
Placed from five detected junctions, three of them on Ridgeway Avenue; residuals are 2 to 8 m and leave-one-out is 8.9 m, so the fit is medium confidence.
West Orange, 100 ft; Ridgeway, Benvenue, Northfield, Prospect; medium

sheet-33.description: Sheet 33 covers a thinly built part of West Orange on the slope south-west of Northfield Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The page is turned so that north lies to the right, which makes the long streets run up and down the sheet. Cable Road runs along the left edge with Bellevue Avenue and Lowell Avenue entering from the west, and Chestnut Avenue, Evergreen Terrace and Cedar Avenue form a small grid of platted blocks at the foot of the sheet beside Gregory Avenue and Wellington Avenue. A few frame dwellings stand on those blocks and along the lower part of Cable Road. Most of the sheet is open ground in large holdings: the estate of Mrs. L. F. F. Wanner, with her house Grey Hurst, fills the centre, and the property of Mrs. C. Roos, with two dwellings, lies on the right beside Mitchell. Northfield Avenue, marked 60 feet wide, crosses the top right corner in a diagonal and bends sharply where it leaves the sheet. At the top left Woodland Boulevard and Cable Road Avenue meet a street leading off the sheet, beside the compass rose. Water pipes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked along Gregory Avenue and Cable Road. Lot lines and parcel numbers are drawn but the great majority of the ground is blank. The neighbouring sheets are named around the edge: 32 above, 34 to the right, 35 at lower right, 36 below and 40 to the left.
notes: Drawn at 100 feet to an inch; the compass rose puts north to the right of the page (about 68 degrees clockwise from up in the fit).
Chestnut Avenue is today Forest Hill Road where it meets Gregory Avenue (junction detected on the drawn lines).
Cedar Avenue appears to be Vossler Terrace today (placed by its spacing from Wellington Avenue; medium confidence).
Mitchell meets Gregory Avenue at the right edge; today that junction is Gregory Avenue / Gregory Place / Mitchell Street, and Mitchell north-west of it is not in the modern street data.
Evergreen Terrace is marked Not Graded.
Today's Prospect Avenue crosses the large Wanner estate in the middle of the sheet but is not drawn on this sheet.
Control is four junctions along Gregory Avenue at the foot of the sheet; the upper two thirds have no control point.
West Orange, 100 ft, turned (north right); one large estate, control only along Gregory Av; medium

sheet-34.description: Sheet 34 shows the wooded slope of West Orange north of Gregory Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the right of the page. Gregory Avenue runs across the foot of the sheet from Mitchell on the left to Northfield Avenue on the right, with water pipes and fire alarm boxes marked along it. Northfield Avenue, 60 feet wide, comes in from the upper left, runs south-east in a long diagonal and then turns down the right side of the sheet to meet Gregory Avenue. Parallel to it at the top is Ridge Road, 40 feet wide, and a 40-foot street with a pipe line branches off to the upper left. Private Road leaves Northfield Avenue on the right in a curve. The ground between these streets is held in large estates and is mostly blank. The property of Jessie E. Koewing, named Berumont, contains a large dwelling drawn in blue (stone) and a group of long parallel frame buildings drawn in yellow, probably greenhouses, with outbuildings; Mary E. Brown owns the land with a single dwelling near Northfield Avenue. Mitchell is a 50-foot street on the left, with its water pipe, running down to Gregory Avenue. Lot lines and lot numbers 57 and 81 are shown but no cross streets. Sheet numbers on the margins identify the neighbours: 32 above, 29 and 30 to the right, 33 to the left and 35 below.
notes: Drawn at 100 feet to an inch; north is toward the right of the page (about 71 degrees clockwise from up in the fit).
Northfield Avenue and Gregory Avenue keep their names today; the drawn bend of Northfield Avenue follows the modern road closely.

Mitchell meets Gregory Avenue at today's Gregory Avenue / Gregory Place / Mitchell Street junction; only that junction and Gregory Avenue / Northfield Avenue are used for control, both detected on the drawn lines.
Ridge Road, Private Road and the stretch of Gregory Avenue west of Mitchell are not in the modern street data.
Berumont, the Koewing estate, has a row of long parallel frame buildings drawn in yellow, probably greenhouses.
West Orange, 100 ft, turned; Gregory / Mitchell and Gregory / Northfield only; helmert, medium

sheet-35.description: Sheet 35 covers the part of West Orange between Northfield Avenue at the top and Wellington Avenue at the bottom, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and slightly turned, with north pointing up and to the left. Gregory Avenue runs down the left side, and Rollinson Street and its short cross places are drawn down the right edge. The upper two thirds of the sheet is open land in large holdings. A private road leaves the left side and rises toward Northfield Avenue; near it stands Mountainside, the house of Kate L. Macy, with its outbuildings. A brook, widened into a small pond in the middle, crosses the sheet from left to right and leaves at the right edge. Mitchell runs across the sheet from Gregory Avenue to Vine, and below it lies the built-up part: Hillside Avenue, Vine and Birch Street are laid out in long narrow lots with frame dwellings along Hillside Avenue and Wellington Avenue, and Hazel Avenue crosses the lower right with Pine Street and Birch Street entering from below. A large pink-coloured brick building stands near Hazel Avenue. Along Rollinson Street the short Riggs, Quimby, Pillot, Olaf and Nutman Places and Mitchell Street enter from the adjoining sheets 46 and 47. Water pipes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked in the streets. Neighbouring sheets named on the margins are 30 and 31 above, 34 and 33 to the left, 36 below and 45, 46 and 47 to the right.
notes: Drawn at 100 feet to an inch; fitted rotation is about -16 degrees.
Vine is today Oakridge Road; Hillside Avenue, Hazel Avenue, Birch Street, Pine Street, Rollinson Street, Wellington Avenue, Gregory Avenue and Mitchell Street keep their names.
Olaf Place is probably today's Osborne Place off Rollinson Street (placed by order along Rollinson Street; medium confidence).
The unnamed brook is labelled only Brook on the sheet.
Mountainside, the house of Kate L. Macy, stands near the private road in the upper middle.
The junction of Hillside Avenue and Wellington Avenue was rejected by the fit (8.7 m) and not used for control.
West Orange, 100 ft; Northfield at top, Hillside / Hazel built-up lower third; high

sheet-36.description: Sheet 36 covers a residential district of West Orange on the slope below the First Mountain, between Gregory Avenue on the west and South Valley Road on the east, from Wellington Avenue at the top of the sheet down to Walker Road at the bottom. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The upper part shows the blocks of Hillside Avenue, Vine, Birch and Pine between Wellington Avenue and Chestnut Avenue, with frame dwellings along Hillside Avenue and Wellington Avenue and a large open block in the middle. Chestnut Avenue crosses the sheet and bends north-east to join South Valley Road. Below it, Cable Road runs parallel to Chestnut Avenue, lined with houses on narrow lots, and Orange Heights Avenue crosses the full width of the sheet. South of Orange Heights Avenue the land is platted into long rows of narrow building lots along Yale Terrace, Harvard Terrace and Oxford Terrace, nearly all still vacant, as is most of the block between Oxford Terrace and South Valley Road apart from one group of buildings. The Bernius Mountainside Hotel stands on South Valley Road near Union Street. At the right edge a brook crosses near Freeman and Forest Street, where the dividing line between the Town of West Orange and the City of Orange is marked; Spruce Street and Nassau Street enter from the adjoining sheet 44. Water pipes with their diameters, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked along the main streets. The blank strip beyond Gregory Avenue at the left belongs to sheets 33 and 40.
notes: Chestnut Avenue is today Forest Hill Road (it bends to meet South Valley Road as drawn).
Cable Road is not in the modern street data between Gregory Avenue and South Valley Road.
Vine and Pine are not on their drawn lines today; they were not used for control.
Bernius Mountainside Hotel on South Valley Road near Union Street.
West Orange, 100 ft to an inch

sheet-37.description: Sheet 37 shows a residential district of West Orange south of Walker Road, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Walker Road runs across the top, and Gregory Avenue runs down the left side from Walker Road to Luddington Avenue at the foot. Lawrence Avenue, with houses on both sides, crosses the upper middle from Overlook Avenue to South Valley, a street along the right edge that curves down the sheet. Ridgeview Avenue runs parallel below it, and Overlook Avenue connects Lawrence and Luddington Avenues. Between Gregory Avenue and Overlook Avenue a block of narrow lots is lined with dwellings. A brook crosses the top between Walker Road and Lawrence Avenue. South of Ridgeview Avenue the land is held in large estates: the Ridgeview Property with a row of outbuildings, T. A. Gillespie with a large house and a green house, T. H. Gillespie with a dwelling drawn in blue, and C. Morgan. J. Campbell owns the land on Walker Road. Edward S. Sanford owns a house beside Luddington Avenue, and Mrs. J. Mandeville a group of buildings below the dash-dot boundary line labelled South Orange Village. Yale Terrace, Harvard Terrace and Oxford Terrace enter from sheet 36 above, and Tremont Avenue and Meeker Street from the right. Water pipes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked along the streets. Neighbouring sheets named on the margins are 36 above, 40 and 39 to the left, 41, 42 and 43 to the right.
notes: Drawn at 100 feet to an inch; fitted rotation is about -28 degrees.
Luddington Avenue is today Luddington Road and South Valley is South Valley Road; the other streets keep their names.
Lawrence Avenue is drawn only as a pipe line west of Overlook Avenue, though today it reaches Gregory Avenue.
Eleven control points, 0.99 m RMSE and 1.5 m leave-one-out; the Luddington Road / South Valley Road junction has the largest residual (2 m).
The Gillespie holdings include a green house.
West Orange, 100 ft; Lawrence / Ridgeview district; high

sheet-38.description: Sheet 38 shows a long wedge of mostly vacant platted land in West Orange between Walker Road on the left and Woodland Boulevard on the right, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The page is turned so that north lies to the right. Walker Road bounds the sheet from the bottom up the left side and curves right across the top. Woodland Boulevard branches from it at the upper right and runs down the right side to Cable Lake at the foot. Five parallel 50-foot streets cross the wedge from Walker Road to Woodland Boulevard: Fairfield Avenue, Wildwood Avenue, Sunset Avenue, Ridgeway Avenue and, at the bottom, Hawthorne Avenue, which meets Walker Road in a curve beside Summit Drive. Between the streets the blocks are divided into narrow lots, numbered with the block numbers 160A to 160H, but almost none is built on; only a few dwellings and outbuildings stand along Sunset Avenue and near Ridgeway Avenue. Cable Lake, a blue-washed pond, lies at the bottom right, and the Summit Drive stub enters from the bottom edge. A dash-dot match line lettered A and B on the left joins this sheet to sheet 39. Neighbouring sheets named on the margins are 12 on the right and at the bottom, 39 and 40 below left, with the margin label 0 at the top and left.
notes: Drawn at 100 feet to an inch; the compass rose puts north to the right of the page (about 87 degrees clockwise from up).
Only Walker Road appears in the modern street data, and it runs along the same line as drawn; none of the cross streets or Woodland Boulevard appears in it.

No street junction exists in the modern data, so the sheet is anchored on one point carried from sheet 39, the extended match line A-B where it meets the west edge of Walker Road, with 100-foot scale and rotation from the compass rose; position and rotation are weak.
The two matching lettered corners A and B of the match line with sheet 39 are drawn on both sheets.
West Orange, 100 ft, turned; vacant platted wedge between Walker Rd and Woodland Blvd; anchored on a point carried from sheet 39, low

sheet-39.description: Sheet 39 covers wooded, thinly settled ground in the west of West Orange, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Walker Road enters at the top right, passing the 50-foot corner where Hawthorne Avenue leaves it, and forks near the right edge where Mountain Avenue joins it. Mountain Avenue curves across the sheet from the right edge, past the estate of S. W. Carey and its dwelling, to a junction at the left of the middle where Lowell Avenue and Luddington Avenue begin, beside the creek. Lowell Avenue runs from that junction east to the right edge, with the properties of C. F. Watson and A. J. McGuire on its south side. Luddington Avenue drops from the junction to Gregory Avenue at the bottom, where Gregory Avenue runs across the foot of the sheet with Lawrence Avenue entering. A brook winds from the top across the middle and down to the left edge. The Town of West Orange ends at the left, where a dash-dot line separates it from South Orange Township and South Orange Village. Large blocks are numbered 43, 44, 45 and 160; the northern part of the sheet is blank. A match line lettered A and B at the top joins sheet 38. Neighbouring sheets named on the margins are 38 above, 40 to the right and 37 below.
notes: Drawn at 100 feet to an inch; fitted rotation is about 63 degrees, with north toward the upper right.
Mountain Avenue is today Mountain Way where it follows the drawn curve; Luddington Avenue is Luddington Road; Lowell Avenue, Walker Road and Gregory Avenue keep their names.

Control is three detected junctions and one hand-picked point (Mountain Way / Walker Road, at the circle 440 mark); the fit has 3.7 m RMSE and no leave-one-out, so placement is low to medium confidence.
In a two-point overlay the modern Lawrence Avenue line falls 20 to 30 m from the drawn one at Gregory Avenue; the junction is kept as one of four control points, with a 5.9 m residual.
The A and B corners of the match line with sheet 38 are drawn at the top.
West Orange, 100 ft, turned; Mountain (today Mountain Way) / Lowell / Luddington estates; four weak points, low

sheet-40.description: Sheet 40 covers the upland district of West Orange between Walker Road on the west and Cable Road on the east, from the loop of Summit Drive at the top of the sheet down to Gregory Avenue along the bottom. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and is turned so that the printed north arrow points to the upper right. Almost all of the sheet is open or platted land. Walker Road enters from Mountain Avenue at the left edge, bends round the sheet and descends to Gregory Avenue, with Lowell Avenue crossing it twice. Orange Heights Avenue winds down from Woodland Boulevard at the top right in long loops, passing the underground City of Orange Distributing Reservoir at the centre, and meets Gregory Avenue near the bottom edge. Bellevue Avenue, Sheffield Terrace and a second Lowell Avenue branch off it towards Cable Road, which runs the full height of the right edge. The only industrial works is the Spottiswoode, Cusack & Co. quarry, shown with its engine house, blacksmith shop, stable and watchman's building, and noted as having no heat, no lights, steam power, coal fuel and one night watchman. A short row of frame dwellings stands on the lots between Walker Road and Lowell Avenue at the left; a few other houses stand on Orange Heights Avenue and near Gregory Avenue. Block numbers 43 to 50 are printed on the unbuilt tracts. Adjoining sheets 33, 36, 37, 38 and 39 are named around the margins.
notes: Printed scale is 100 feet to an inch; the fitted scale of about 3.95 pixels per foot agrees.
Summit Drive, Bellevue Avenue, Cable Road and Woodland Boulevard are not in the modern street data under these names.
The winding street drawn as Orange Heights Avenue north of Gregory Avenue is Winding Way today; the modern Orange Heights Avenue is the stretch below Gregory Avenue.
Walker Road and Lowell Avenue cross twice on the sheet about 73 m apart, but the two modern crossings are about 41 m apart; neither was used for control.
The Mountain Avenue fork at the left edge was hand-picked and matched to Mountain Way / Walker Road.
West Orange, 100 ft; Walker Rd, Orange Heights, Gregory; quarry and reservoir; medium

sheet-41.description: Sheet 41 shows the south-west corner of West Orange where it meets South Orange and the City of Orange, between South Valley at the top and Valley at the bottom. The printed scale bar reads 100 feet to an inch, but the fitted scale, the street spacing and the street widths all correspond to 50 feet to an inch. A brook, marked as the boundary line between the Town of West Orange and the City of Orange, crosses the sheet from the left edge and bends down towards the right; a vertical dash-dot line along the left edge is the boundary of the Village of South Orange.
