North of the brook the sheet is almost empty: long platted lots lie along Hillside Place, which is marked not graded, below South Valley. South of the brook Luddington Avenue, Argyle Avenue and Morris cross the district and end at Valley; the blocks between them are plotted in narrow lots with a few frame dwellings, a carpenter shop with a gasoline engine, and outbuildings, mostly on the Argyle Avenue and Valley frontages. A water main marked with 12 inch and 20 inch pipes runs along Valley, and East Clark Place leaves Valley to the south at the left. Blocks 64 and 65 south of Valley, sheet 37 to the north and sheet 42 to the east are named in the margins. A scale bar and a north arrow stand in the lower left and upper right.
notes: The printed scale bar says 100 feet to an inch, but the sheet fits 8.0 pixels per foot, which is 50 feet to an inch; Valley is labelled 50 feet wide and spans about 400 pixels.
Control is only three points along Valley (Morris, Argyle and McLaughlin Place / East Clark Place), so the part is placed as a two-parameter similarity and rotation is taken from Valley alone.
Luddington Avenue, Hillside Place and the Hillside Place blocks have no modern counterpart in the street data.
Valley is Valley Street today; East Clark Place meets it at the modern McLaughlin Place.
West Orange, drawn at 50 ft although the bar says 100 ft; South Valley / Valley at the South Orange and Orange lines; helmert along Valley, low

sheet-42.description: Sheet 42 covers the district round the Chestnut Street and Valley crossing on the boundary of West Orange and the City of Orange, at 50 feet to an inch. South Valley crosses the top of the sheet, Valley the bottom, Tremont Avenue the right side and Morris the left. Meeker runs north from the pumping station as the main street of the upper half and carries the name Chestnut below the brook; Ridgeview Avenue and Lawrence Avenue enter from the top. The upper blocks hold rows of frame dwellings along Meeker, Central 2 Pl. and South Valley, with a church called Ridgeview Chapel with its heating and lighting noted, a wagon shed and a stream in a narrow channel running down through the middle blocks. A brook, marked as the boundary between the Town of West Orange and the City of Orange, crosses the middle of the sheet beside the South Orange and Maplewood Traction Co. right of way. South of it the large City of Orange Pumping Station (water and sewage) and Electric Light Station, with its coal shed, occupies the block at Chestnut and Beech; it is marked as running day and night and without a watchman. Dwellings stand along Valley and along Tremont Avenue, and a concrete company's office and storage building for building materials stands on the Central 2 Pl. block. Sheets 37, 41, 43, 65 and 66 are named in the margins.
notes: The street printed Beech is Beach Street today.
Meeker and Chestnut are one street on the sheet; the modern street data changes name at Chestnut Street / Meeker Street, which was not detected.
Central 2 Pl. is printed with the numeral 2; it is Central Place today.
Valley is Valley Street today.
West Orange, 50 ft; Chestnut, Meeker, Valley, pumping station; high

sheet-43.description: Sheet 43 shows the part of West Orange and the City of Orange around the upper end of Valley, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that Valley runs up the page and the printed north arrow points to the upper left. Union runs across the top of the sheet and Tremont Avenue across the bottom; South Valley curves down the left edge and meets Walker Rd at the bottom left. A brook runs from top to bottom in a narrow channel along the middle of the sheet, together with the South Orange and Maplewood Traction Co. right of way, and the boundary between the Town of West Orange and the City of Orange is marked along it. West of the brook two broad blocks, divided by Freeman 3 Pl., are platted into long rows of narrow lots, almost all vacant; a few dwellings and a coop stand near Union. East of it the blocks between Liberty and Valley, bounded by Union above and W. Christopher below, are closely built with frame dwellings, stores, an undertaker's and a plumber's shop; Mc Chesney St. and Christopher St. run east from Valley, and a livery stable and its outbuildings stand on the block at the bottom right. Water mains are marked along Valley, Union and Tremont Avenue. Sheets 36, 37, 42, 44, 66 and 67 are named in the margins.
notes: The sheet is turned: its fitted rotation is about -22 degrees, against about +70 for sheet 42, which adjoins it at the bottom.
Valley is Valley Street today; South Valley is South Valley Road.
The street printed Mc Chesney St. is McChesney Street today.
Freeman 3 Pl. is printed with the numeral 3; it is Freeman Place today.
West Orange, 50 ft, turned; Valley, Union, Liberty, Freeman; high

sheet-44.description: Sheet 44 shows the Valley district of West Orange and the City of Orange along Valley, Freeman and Forest, at 50 feet to an inch. The sheet is turned like its neighbour 43, with Valley running up the page along the right side. Freeman runs from the bend of South Valley at the centre up to the street across the top, which is lettered Wellington Av. at the left and Freeman at the right; Forest crosses the middle of the sheet to Valley, and Nassau and Union cross the lower part. A brook runs down from the top between Spruce and Freeman and joins the boundary stream that marks the line between the Town of West Orange and the City of Orange, which crosses the lower half of the sheet. The upper right blocks hold frame dwellings, with the Forest St. Public School, a large brick building in pink with its heating and lighting noted, set back from Freeman; a strip lettered Park lies beside Valley. In the middle the Public Service Corp. of N.J. Street Railway Dept. car barns stand at the junction of Chestnut Av. and South Valley. Lower down are the blocks on Austin Pl. and Nassau, with dwellings and shops, Lyceum Hall with a bowling alley, Our Lady of the Valley School annex and the Cable Road Hotel with its sheds, at the bottom. The left side is largely platted lots on Pine, Spruce and Wellington Av. Sheets 36, 37, 38, 43, 45, 67 and 68 are named in the margins.
notes: Valley is Valley Street today; South Valley is South Valley Road.
Spruce is Rollinson Street today, judged from its junction with Wellington Avenue.
The detector placed South Valley Road / Wellington Avenue 45 ft off on an inner line; it was replaced by a hand-picked point on the pipe crossing.
Chestnut Av. here is the street that meets South Valley at the car barns; it is Forest Hill Road further west on sheet 36.
West Orange, 50 ft, turned; Valley, Forest, Freeman, Nassau; high

sheet-45.description: Sheet 45 covers a residential district at the north-east end of West Orange and the City of Orange along Hazel Av. and Valley, at 50 feet to an inch. The sheet is turned, with the printed north arrow pointing to the upper right and Wellington Av. running up the left side. Birch, Pine, Spruce and Cross run across it, Freeman marks the edge of the City of Orange at the lower left, and Hazel Av. runs diagonally from the top down to Valley at the bottom. Mitchell runs up the right side, and Rollinson St. is lettered at the upper right. Large blocks at the top are divided into building lots, mostly vacant. The Hazel Av. Public School, a pink brick building with its heating, lighting and queen chemical extinguishers noted, stands to the right of Hazel Av. A brook crosses the middle of the sheet beside the South Orange & Maplewood Traction Co. right of way, then turns north-east beside Hazel Av. Below it, dwellings fill the blocks along Cross, with houses numbered from 3 to 31 on one side and 2 to 28 on the other, and along Valley at the bottom, where a stucco house and a plumber's shop stand at the corner of Freeman. East of Hazel Av. the lots on Mitchell are closely built with frame dwellings, and F. E. Pearce's garage and repair shop stands at the lower right. Sheets 27, 29, 30, 31, 35, 36, 44, 46 and 69 are named around the margins.
notes: Spruce is Rollinson Street today and Birch Street, Pine Street and Wellington Avenue keep their names; this was fixed from their spacing from Wellington Avenue's junction with South Valley Road.
Valley is Valley Street / Valley Road today.
The Cross Street / Freeman Street junction was left out: the detector's point and a hand pick at the middle of Freeman both sat 3 to 4 m from the fit of the other points.
Block numbers 27 to 31 are printed on the unbuilt tracts at the top.
West Orange, 50 ft; Hazel Av, Cross, Valley, Wellington; high

sheet-46.description: Sheet 46 lies in the village district of West Orange at 50 feet to an inch. It is bounded by Rollinson on the left edge, Quimby Place along the top, Mitchell along the bottom and Valley, which runs up the right-hand side as a long straight street. Pillot Place, Olaf Place, Nutman Place and Central Avenue run across the sheet to Valley, and Joyce Street meets Valley at the right edge below the Kingsley Street corner. The sheet is mostly platted but thinly built: frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys stand along Quimby, Pillot, Nutman and Mitchell and in a row on the Valley side, while the large blocks numbered 23 to 26 between the cross streets are largely vacant lots, several marked Not Graded. A curved right of way of the South Orange and Maplewood Traction Co. crosses the sheet from the upper right toward the lower left and bends the blocks around it. An unnamed stream enters at the left edge and runs down the sheet to meet the traction line near Nutman Place. Water pipes (4 inch, 6 inch) are lettered along the streets, with a fire alarm box at Valley and Joyce Street, and street widths of 50 and 60 feet are marked. The scale bar and the Map Division stamp are at the bottom. Adjoining sheets are 47 above, 45 below, 35 on the left, and 48, 69 and 71 on the right.
notes: Valley, as printed, appears to be modern Valley Road here (fit to modern junctions); sheet 48 continues it north.
Quimby, Pillot, Nutman and Central keep their names today as Quimby Place, Pillot Place, Nutman Place and Central Avenue; Mitchell is Mitchell Street.
Olaf Place is not in OpenStreetMap and was not used as control.
Rollinson Street along the left edge is cut by the scan edge and was not used as control, so every control point lies on Valley and the fit is a similarity (low to medium confidence).
West Orange, 50 ft; Rollinson to Valley, Quimby to Mitchell; control only along Valley, medium-low

sheet-47.description: Sheet 47 shows the blocks east of Rollinson, in the village district of West Orange, at 50 feet to an inch. Rollinson runs down the left side of the sheet. Four streets cross the sheet from it toward the right edge, where they continue onto sheet 48: Whittingham Place along the top, then Swaine Place, Riggs Place and Quimby Place along the bottom. Northfield Avenue crosses the upper left corner on a diagonal, and a 60 foot street width is marked on it. Long narrow lots with frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys fill the blocks between Swaine, Riggs and Quimby, many with small outbuildings, coops and sheds, and a few carpenter shops; block numbers 20, 21 and 22 appear. A small brick or concrete building stands near the top left. An unnamed stream runs from Northfield Avenue across the upper blocks to the right edge. Lots are numbered with house numbers along each street, and water pipes (4 inch and 6 inch) are lettered along the cross streets. A compass rose and north arrow are at the left, and the scale bar and Map Division stamp at the bottom. A right of way is lettered at the lower right below Quimby Place. Adjoining sheets are 31 above left, 49 above right, 35 on the left, 48 on the right and 46 below.
notes: Northfield Av. at the upper left is probably the street now called Old Northfield Avenue or Northfield Avenue; it was not used as control.
Kingsley Street, just beyond the right edge, is not lettered on this sheet.
Control points lie only on Rollinson Street, so the fit is a similarity (low to medium confidence); the cross axis rests on the scale and rotation measured along that line.
West Orange, 50 ft; Rollinson, Whittingham to Quimby; control only along Rollinson, medium-low

sheet-48.description: Sheet 48 covers the Kingsley Street and Valley district of West Orange at 50 feet to an inch. Kingsley runs down the left-centre of the sheet and is crossed by Whittingham Place at the top, Swaine Place, Riggs Place and Quimby Place; Wheeler Street enters at the top from sheet 49. A diagonal right of way lettered South Orange and Maplewood Traction Co. Right of Way cuts across from the lower left to the upper right, and a lettered brook runs from the left edge through the middle of the sheet and down to the lower right. On the right side, Valley runs up the sheet as a wide curving street, with Glebe Street and Cary Street meeting it from the right and Dean Street below; Valley Street is lettered at the bottom edge. The largest features are a Fire Department building, Fire House No. 1, near the top right with an old fire house beside it, and a large open area marked Play Ground between the traction line and Valley. West of Kingsley the blocks hold frame dwellings with outbuildings on narrow lots; east of it the lots are largely vacant, some marked Not Graded. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inch are shown along the streets. A compass rose is at the lower right and the scale bar and Map Division stamp at the bottom. Adjoining sheets are 49 above, 47 on the left, 46 below, 71 and 73.
notes: Valley, as printed, appears to be modern Valley Road; it carries the fire station at its upper end.
Glebe Street, Cary Street and Dean Street survive as Glebe Street, Cary Street and Dean Street; Kingsley is Kingsley Street today.
Control rests on Kingsley Street and the Whittingham Place and Valley junction; leave-one-out is not meaningful with so few points.
Kingsley appears here without a suffix as printed.
West Orange, 50 ft; Kingsley and Valley, fire house, playground; medium

sheet-49.description: Sheet 49 lies in the village district of West Orange at 50 feet to an inch and is turned about 76 degrees, so that north points toward the right of the page (the compass is at the upper right). Valley runs along the bottom of the sheet, with Whittingham Place rising from it at the left and Northfield Avenue running up the right side. Northfield Avenue also appears as a long street across the top. Wheeler crosses the lower third from Whittingham Place to Northfield Avenue, and Kingsley Street meets Whittingham Place at the left edge. Gaston Street is lettered at the right where it meets Northfield Avenue. Along Valley the lots are small and closely built, with rows of frame dwellings, a number of sheds, and at the lower right a garage of brick or concrete, a plumber, a post office and other stores, some drawn in pink for brick. The large central block, numbered 19, is mostly open with a few dwellings and a small building near its top. Block numbers 17 and 19 are shown, and 6 inch and 8 inch water pipes are lettered along Whittingham Place, Wheeler and Valley. The scale bar and Map Division stamp are at the lower left and bottom. Adjoining sheets are 47 and 31 above, 48 on the left, 50 on the right and 74 below.
notes: Valley, as printed, appears to be modern Valley Road; the bottom-right corner is the Valley and Northfield junction.
Northfield Av. is Northfield Avenue today; Wheeler is Wheeler Street.
Gaston Street at the right edge was not used as control.
Four control points, at Kingsley and Whittingham, Wheeler and Northfield, Valley and Northfield, and Valley and Whittingham; the sheet is turned about 76 degrees from the usual orientation.
West Orange, 50 ft, turned; Whittingham, Wheeler, Valley; medium

sheet-50.description: Sheet 50 shows the centre of the village district of West Orange at 50 feet to an inch, between Mount Pleasant Avenue at the top and Northfield Avenue at the bottom. Valley, a wide curving street, runs up the right side and Main Street meets it at the bottom right near the Fire Alarm box. Gaston is on the left, Wheeler runs down the middle, and Lindsley Avenue curves across the centre from Gaston to Valley. Fairmount Avenue and Condit cut diagonally across the upper right, and Condit Terrace and White Street are lettered at the left and top right. The principal buildings are West Orange High School, a large pink brick building lettered with heat, steam and furnace, lights and gas, in the upper left block (68), and the Municipal Building with cells in the lower right block (69). Along Valley and Lindsley Avenue stand stores, a hay and grain dealer and plumber, drug and auto supply shops, a laundry and a burned out building; the blocks to the left hold frame dwellings in a regular grid of lots, and the upper right holds scattered dwellings. Block numbers 67 to 70 are shown. A compass rose is at the right, and the scale bar and Map Division stamp at the bottom. Adjoining sheets are 51 above, 31 on the left, 49 below and 103 on the right.
notes: Valley north of Northfield Avenue is modern Main Street in OpenStreetMap; the junction labelled Main St. at the lower right is Northfield Avenue and Valley Road.

Gaston as printed is not matched to the modern Gaston Street: the modern junction of Gaston Street, Laird Drive and Lindsley Avenue lies about 30 m from where the sheet draws Gaston meeting Lindsley, so it was left out of the control.
Mt. Pleasant Av. is Mount Pleasant Avenue today.
West Orange, 50 ft; Lindsley, Wheeler, Valley, high school and municipal building; medium

sheet-51.description: Sheet 51 shows the northern end of the village district of West Orange at 50 feet to an inch and is turned about 86 degrees, with north toward the right of the page (the compass is at the upper right). Mount Pleasant Avenue runs up the left side of the sheet from the bottom left corner, where it meets Valley. Valley runs along the bottom, with Llewellyn Place rising from it at the right and the curve of Park Way at the bottom right. Wildwood Avenue crosses the top, and Wildwood Way curves down the right side from it. Park Place runs from Mount Pleasant Avenue toward the top, and Gaston Street meets Mount Pleasant Avenue near the upper left. Condit and Fairmount Avenue are lettered at the left edge, and White Street at the left near the bottom. A brook crosses the middle of the sheet from the upper right to the lower left and passes through the works of the C. B. Rutan Co., hat manufacturers, a large complex of pink brick buildings with a blowing room, forming and pouncing and finishing rooms, a coal pile and a dye house; St. Mark's Public School stands beside it. A frame dwelling lettered Overbrook, C. R. Browning, stands at the right, and Pine Bend, A. J. Lenner, near the centre. Block number 88 covers the large central parcel. The scale bar and Map Division stamp are at the bottom. Adjoining sheets are 28 above, 50 on the left, 52 and 26 on the right and 112 below.
notes: Valley here continues modern Main Street in OpenStreetMap; the junction at the lower left corner is Mount Pleasant Avenue and Main Street.
Mt. Pleasant Av. is Mount Pleasant Avenue today.

Llewellyn Place and Main Street meet at the bottom edge; that junction was not detected and its modern node does not agree with the pipe junction drawn on the sheet, so it was left out of the control.

Three control points on Mount Pleasant Avenue (Main Street junction hand-picked from the water pipe crossing), so the fit is a similarity with fitted scale 3 percent above the atlas value (low to medium confidence).
West Orange, 50 ft, turned; Mount Pleasant / Valley, Rutan hat works; helmert, low-medium

sheet-52.description: Sheet 52 covers the Valley Street district of West Orange, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points toward the lower right. Valley, a diagonal street, divides the sheet. West of it a long block of frame dwellings, mostly two and a half storey, stands on narrow deep lots between Valley and Edgehill Avenue; a boarding house is marked on the west side, and the block below Valley carries a greenhouse range with a gate house on the lot behind it. Honeysuckle Avenue crosses the top left, with Lakeside Avenue along the top edge. East of Valley, the largest feature is the plant of the Edison Storage Battery Co., two long parallel brick and concrete buildings, one marked as fireproof construction and the other as the storage battery manufacturing building, with the platting building between them, on the block bounded by Lakeside Avenue, Valley, Charles and Ashland Avenue. South of Charles the block between Valley and Ashland Avenue holds dwellings, small shops and a small building shaded blue. Park Way and Park Avenue run along the bottom edge, where a curved street line from sheet 51 enters the corner. Water mains, hydrants, lot numbers and building heights are marked throughout. A compass rose and the Princeton library stamp occupy the lower right, and the area east of Ashland Avenue is blank, belonging to sheet 115. Adjoining sheets are numbered 24, 26, 53 and 112 in the margins.
notes: Valley is today Main Street; Charles is today Charles Street.
Edge Hill Av. and Edgehill Av. are both printed, the first as a short diagonal street at the left edge and the second along the left side of the main block.
Edison Storage Battery Co. plant is the large orange-shaded complex east of Valley.
West Orange, 50 ft; Valley (today Main Street), Charles, Ashland, Edison Storage Battery works; medium

sheet-53-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 53 is the left part of the sheet, west of a heavy vertical dividing line, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. It is almost entirely taken up by the Edison Phonograph Works and Edison's Laboratory in West Orange, filling the block between Valley along the top, Lakeside Avenue on the left, Alden on the right and Watchung Avenue at the bottom. At the top are the laboratory group, numbered 1 to 10: the library, lecture room and machine shop, galvanometer, chemical laboratory, oil house, carpenter shop and moulding house, with a note on the laboratory's watchmen, sprinklers and private fire department. Below them stand the large reinforced concrete buildings of the works: the general office, the Record Manufacturing Plant, the moulding and testing building, wax making and wax houses, cabinet manufacturing and assembling, the auto garage and chemical laboratory, stock room and phonograph packing, the blacksmith shop, tool making and film plant, the punch presses and film storage, the packing room, store room, grind shop, oil house, boiler house with its chimneys, the engine house with the electric plant, and primary battery manufacturing. Rail sidings cross the works. In the lower left the Erie Railroad Orange Branch and a brook run past a row of small dwellings and saloons, and the boundary line between the Town of West Orange and the City of Orange crosses Watchung Avenue. Ashland Avenue meets Lakeside Avenue on the left; Columbia Street and Liberty Street enter at the right. Notes give the works' watch service, sprinkler system and private fire department.
notes: Valley is today Main Street.
Edison Laboratory and the Edison Phonograph Works (Thomas A. Edison).
Three of the five control points are hand-picked from water pipes and block corners at Watchung Avenue and Ashland Avenue, where the street edges are not drawn.

West Orange, 50 ft; two parts split by a heavy vertical line: part 1 (left) Edison Phonograph Works between Valley, Lakeside Av and Alden; part 2 (right) Alden St / Watchung Av / High St strip at the Orange line

sheet-53-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 53 is the right part of the sheet, east of a heavy vertical dividing line, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. It continues the area south of the Edison works in West Orange: Alden runs down the right side from Watchung Avenue at the top to High at the bottom, with Bradford Street leaving it to the east. Along the left side the Erie Railroad Orange Branch runs down the part beside an open brook. Watchung Avenue crosses the top, where the boundary line between the Town of West Orange and the City of Orange runs diagonally across the street. The block between the railroad and Alden is lined with frame dwellings and flats on Alden and Watchung Avenue, with yards, coops and outbuildings behind. At the bottom, on High, stand the H. W. Bulkley Iron Works with a brick machine shop and a frame building. Water pipes, hydrants and house numbers are marked along the streets. Blank ground to the right of Alden belongs to sheet 54, which is in the other volume of this series.
notes: Placed from three junctions along Alden Street (Watchung Avenue, Bradford Street, High Street): a helmert fit, medium to low confidence.
H. W. Bulkley Iron Works on High.

West Orange, 50 ft; two parts split by a heavy vertical line: part 1 (left) Edison Phonograph Works between Valley, Lakeside Av and Alden; part 2 (right) Alden St / Watchung Av / High St strip at the Orange line

sheet-55.description: Sheet 55 shows the centre of the West Orange business district, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points toward the lower right. Valley, a main street, runs down the left edge. Along its east side between Washington and Kling stand the stores of the village: a drug store, hardware store, bakery and shops, with the West Orange Fire Department Hose Company No. 2 and its wagon house behind them, and the corner of Prospect Place at the left edge. Behind the stores, in the block between Washington and Kling, the West Orange Presbyterian Church stands at the centre, with dwellings and a small frame building shaded blue along the lower edge of the block. Below Kling the Hotel Wellington faces Valley, with dwellings and its stable to the east. Babcock Place crosses the lower half, and Alden runs along the bottom edge with Edisonia Tr. entering Valley at the lower left. A band of dwellings lines both sides of Columbia on the right, with Liberty at the right edge, and the lower right corner holds the Edison Phonograph Works, marked to be seen on sheet 53. Water pipes, hydrants, a fire alarm box and a compass rose are shown, and the blocks near the centre are only thinly built.
notes: Valley is today Main Street; Kling is today Kling Street; Babcock Place and Alden keep their names (Alden Street).
The Edison Phonograph Works at the lower right is marked 'see sheet 53' on the sheet.
West Orange village centre, 50 ft; Valley (today Main Street), Washington, Kling, Babcock, Alden; high

sheet-56.description: Sheet 56 covers the southeast edge of the village of West Orange, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points toward the lower right. Liberty forms the left side and Bradford the right side, with Watchung Avenue running down the middle and Alden along the bottom. Washington crosses the top as a broad diagonal street with Meade Street and Burnside Street entering its south side, and Condit Lane meets it at the top near Watchung Avenue. A brook, shaded blue, flows from the top left down the left half of the sheet and ends at the works of the Edison Gas Co., drawn in orange at the bottom, where it is labelled as providing heat, steam, light and electricity from its main power plant. Narrow lots of frame dwellings, most with two storeys, line both sides of Watchung Avenue and the west side of Liberty. A broken line crossing the sheet from lower left to upper right marks the boundary between the Town of West Orange and the City of Orange, and the large block east of it, numbered 203, is almost empty, with dwellings only along its edges and a row of houses facing Alden. Block numbers, water pipes, hydrants and a compass rose are shown; the stamp of the Princeton University Library is at the lower right. Neighbouring sheets are 53, 54, 55, 58 and 61.
notes: Printed streets match modern Washington Street, Liberty Street, Watchung Avenue, Condit Lane, Alden Street and Bradford Street. Meade Street and Burnside Street are in the drawn area but not part of the georeferencing control.
The brook is labelled simply 'Brook'; the town boundary line is lettered 'Boundary Line, Town of West Orange, City of Orange'.
West Orange, 50 ft; Liberty, Watchung Av, Bradford, Washington, Alden; medium

sheet-57-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 57 is the upper part of the sheet, above a heavy horizontal dividing line, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. It covers a district of West Orange east of Main Street, between Eagle Rock Avenue and Valley Street at the top, Washington on the left, Ridge Avenue on the right and Whittlesey Avenue near the bottom. Most of the large block between Washington, Eagle Rock Avenue, Franklin Avenue and Whittlesey Avenue is the grounds of the Washington St. Public School, a long brick building with an auditorium, with notes on its heating, lighting and fire equipment; a brook runs down through the grounds. Frame dwellings and a few flats stand along Whittlesey Avenue and on both sides of William between Franklin Avenue and Whittlesey Avenue, with more houses facing Ridge Avenue. Llewellyn Avenue enters at the top beside Eagle Rock Avenue, and William Street continues north of Franklin Avenue. Below Whittlesey Avenue the part shows only the outlines of the blocks drawn in full on sheet 58, with Columbia Street and John Street. Water pipes with their sizes, hydrants, a fire alarm box at Ridge Avenue and house numbers are marked. The lower part of the sheet, below the dividing line, is part 2.
notes: Valley Street is today Main Street.

sheet-57-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 57 is the lower part of the sheet, below a heavy horizontal dividing line, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. It shows two residential blocks of West Orange between Franklin Avenue at the top and Whittlesey Avenue at the bottom, from Ridge Avenue on the left across Birch and Cherry to Chestnut at the right edge. The block between Ridge Avenue and Birch has frame dwellings and flats along Franklin Avenue and Whittlesey Avenue, with a saloon at the corner of Ridge Avenue and Whittlesey Avenue and coops and sheds behind. The blocks between Birch, Cherry and Chestnut are only partly built, with a few dwellings and many vacant lots. Streets are drawn 50 feet wide; water pipes, hydrants, a fire alarm box at Ridge Avenue and Franklin Avenue, and house numbers are marked. Ground above Franklin Avenue is blank, belonging to sheet 20. The upper part of the sheet is part 1.
notes: Four of the five control points are hand-picked from the drawn block corners: Chestnut and Ridge Avenue are cut by the sheet edges and the detector placed them a block-width off.

sheet-58.description: Sheet 58 shows a residential district of West Orange between Ridge Avenue at the top and Washington at the bottom, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Four long north-south blocks are cut by Whittlesey Avenue on the left, Watson Avenue, High and Watchung Avenue on the right. The blocks are almost entirely made up of narrow frame dwellings, many of two and a half storeys, with coops and sheds behind. At the top the First M. E. Church stands on the corner of Ridge Avenue and High. John crosses the top of the left block, and below it a brook, shaded blue, winds down the west side of the block between Whittlesey Avenue and Watson Avenue and passes under Washington. William Street is a fragment entering the left edge and Columbia Street runs down the lower left. Washington crosses the bottom with a stretch of curved street, and Liberty runs south from it. On the right a wedge between Watchung Avenue and Condit Lane is only partly platted, and the Rosedale Cemetery lies along the right edge, with a house and outbuildings inside. A compass rose and the Princeton library stamp fill the lower right. Water pipes, hydrants, a fire alarm box and block numbers are marked. Adjoining sheets are numbered 55, 56, 57, 59, 61.
notes: Printed names match modern Ridge Avenue, Whittlesey Avenue, William Street, John Street, Watson Avenue, High Street, Watchung Avenue, Washington Street, Liberty Street, Columbia Street and Condit Lane.
The brook is labelled simply 'Brook'.

sheet-59.description: Sheet 59 shows a long residential district of West Orange between Chestnut at the top and Ridge Avenue at the bottom, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Whittlesey Avenue, Watson Avenue, High and Watchung Avenue run down the sheet and divide it into three long blocks and a strip along the right. Narrow deep lots are drawn in regular rows on every block, with frame dwellings, many of two and a half storeys, along the street fronts and coops and sheds behind. The densest building is on the left block along Whittlesey Avenue and Watson Avenue, where a bakery, shaded pink, stands near the middle, and the blocks between Watson Avenue and Watchung Avenue are thinly built, with large areas of vacant lots, a few foundations and an auto house shown. Cherry Street and Birch Street are shown as stubs at the left edge, west of Whittlesey Avenue, where the paper is damaged. Rosedale Cemetery runs along the right edge. Water pipes, hydrants, fire alarm boxes, lot numbers and block numbers are marked. A compass rose is at the top and a scale of feet at the lower left. The adjoining sheets are numbered 57, 58 and 60, and the Princeton University Library stamp is at the bottom.
notes: Printed names match modern Chestnut Street, Whittlesey Avenue, Watson Avenue, High Street, Watchung Avenue, Ridge Avenue, Cherry Street and Birch Street.
West Orange, 50 ft; Chestnut to Ridge between Whittlesey and Watchung; high

sheet-60.description: Sheet 60 shows the northeast edge of West Orange, next to the Town of Montclair, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points toward the right. Chestnut forms the left edge, with Franklin Avenue at the top, Whittlesey Avenue, Watson Avenue, High and Watchung Avenue running to the right across the sheet, and Enfield Avenue continuing Watchung Avenue to the lower right. Narrow lots with frame dwellings, mostly two and a half storeys, line the streets close to Chestnut, while the ground toward the right is thinly built. Elm Street and Maple Street cut off the top edge. Hilltop Place runs diagonally from the top right to the lower right edge and Amelia lies beyond it. The broken line of the Town of Montclair boundary crosses the right half, and within the wedge between it and Hilltop Place stand an Essex Fells dairy and its outbuildings, with houses along the street. A group of dwellings lies in the bottom left corner above the Rosedale Cemetery, whose lettering runs along the bottom edge. The north arrow and the Princeton University Library stamp are at the lower right, with a scale of feet below. Block numbers, water pipes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked. Neighbouring sheets are 20, 57 and 59.
notes: Printed names match modern Franklin Avenue, Whittlesey Avenue, Watson Avenue, High Street, Watchung Avenue, Enfield Avenue, Hilltop Place, Amelia Street and Chestnut Street.
Chestnut is cut off by the left edge, so its lettering is only partly visible.
The 'Essex Fells Dairy' stands near Hilltop Place, close to the Town of Montclair line.
